# Eizport — full documentation

> Eizport gives Tools → Export a new screen and .wxrz bundles: content with its media, settings and post content files in one file. Choose items and what they use comes along as suggestions; import with the WordPress Importer, or send the file as a plugin that imports itself. Free and open source.

Version 1.1.0. Requires WordPress 7.0+ and PHP 7.4+.

---

## What's new in 1.1.0

- Added: Playground options: a Language group — the Playground .zip opens in the site's language (the default), yours or English, with the translations of WordPress, the themes and the plugins (fetched from WordPress.org, or this site's inside the .zip).
- Added: Block themes: templates and template parts edited in the Site Editor on rows of their own (Editor templates, Editor template parts), item by item with a preview. They travel in the WXR with the images they use; on import each replaces the same template of the same theme instead of adding a copy ("Header 2"), and its navigations, images and links point to the ones on the other site.
- Added: Elementor, with its own exporter and importer: a row of its own exports the site settings (the Kit) and templates in Elementor's formats; pages built with Elementor carry their design as post_content/<slug>.json; on import, Elementor's own import brings them in, with the images the bundle brought, templates and links pointing to the items there, and a later delivery updates instead of adding copies; also in Playground.
- Added: Advanced Custom Fields (ACF): a row of its own exports its post types, taxonomies and field groups in ACF's own export format, imported before the content (updated by key); the fields that store IDs (image, file, post object, relationship, page link, taxonomy, user) are remapped on import, also in Playground; field groups, linked posts and the media of image and file fields are suggested or come along.
- Added: Bundles say which Eizport made them and the oldest that reads them: a bundle that needs a newer Eizport is refused with a message that says which version (on the upload, wp eizport import, the import ability and a bundle plugin's screen, which offers Update now); bundles from 1.0.x still import. The WordPress Importer must be 0.9.6 or newer; a version newer than the tested one imports with a warning. The manifest names its JSON Schema (https://eizport.github.io/schemas/1.1/manifest.json): editors check a manifest edited by hand, and the import checks it against the same schema.
- Added: Multisite: each site of a network exports and imports on its own — saved defaults per site, files in the site's uploads, links mapped between subsites — and uninstalling cleans every site.
- Added: Export the site's look on rows of its own, item by item — Customizer theme mods and custom CSS rules, the Site Editor's style groups and CSS rules, widgets (classic and block) — with a preview of each and the media they use. On import, CSS rules are added to the other site's CSS (at the end, at the start, or replacing it) between head/tail comments named after the file; theme mods, style groups and widgets join the other site's instead of replacing them.
- Added: Export navigation menus on their own row — classic menus with their items and theme locations, and block navigations — and bring them back on import, pointing to the imported pages.
- Added: Playground options: must-use plugins — the ones chosen go in the Playground .zip with the folders they load, and the blueprint writes them before the import (not the platform's loaders nor Eizport's own).
- Added: Playground options: the button (renamed from "Themes and plugins") also sets where the Playground .zip opens — the home page, the dashboard, a page of the site (as a relative path) or a path —, its two groups open one at a time.
- Changed: The plugin's row on the Plugins screen keeps only Settings: no "Import .wxrz" or "Install the WordPress Importer" link — importing starts from Tools → Import.
- Changed: A bundle plugin's screen is one screen, with or without Eizport: Eizport is one more line in Before importing (Install Now, Activate or Update now, done right there), and what needs it waits — What it holds dimmed, Update existing and Run import disabled. The screen is no longer an item under Tools: Run import, on the plugin's row on the Plugins screen, opens it. Tools → Import lists it too, set apart from the other importers, and shows the list while it waits. "Update existing" names the content types the export holds — on the Export screen, the importer's step 1 and a bundle plugin's screen — and isn't offered with none.
- Changed: The Options row's Basics and Appearance groups no longer carry the theme mods (they have their own row) and now carry the block themes' site logo; imported theme mods are merged into the site's instead of replacing them.
- Changed: What a file holds no longer decides on its own: an import sets the options of the groups, the theme mods and the widgets, and any other option in the file only when whoever imports checks it (step 1 of the importer, a bundle plugin's screen) or names it (--options, the ability's options); WP-CLI and the ability update existing items only when asked. Options, theme mods and widget fields named like secrets (passwords, tokens, API and license keys) are never exported nor listed. On a network, a site administrator's Playground .zip takes only the plugins active on that site and the themes it may use.
- Changed: Bundles are plain .zip files by default (Settings → Export → "Bundle as .zip" now on), inside a plugin made as plugin too; turned off, they are .wxrz as before.
- Fixed: Imported content keeps working with its media and pages: the IDs in Image, Gallery, Cover, Media & Text, File, Video and Audio blocks, in navigation links and in block widgets point to the imported items, not to the other site's.
- Fixed: Links to the source site in imported content — pages, products, categories, navigation links, menus' custom links, widgets — point to this site after an import, in new and updated items.
- Fixed: An attachment the site already has gets its URLs in the imported content pointed to the file here on every import, not only with "Update existing" on.
- Fixed: Checked with the WordPress Importer 0.9.7: an edited image's link to its original is mapped on import instead of dropped (or left pointing at the exporting site's ID with 0.9.6).
- Fixed: The Playground .zip installs a theme or plugin from the WordPress.org directory only in a version the directory has; a development, beta or RC copy goes inside the .zip. Without Eizport, a bundle plugin installs it from the plugin directory.
- Fixed: An export of chosen types carries its terms in full — description, parent and term meta (a product category's thumbnail and display type), with their ancestors — not only their names.
- Fixed: The Playground .zip installs plugins active or inactive as they are on the site, instead of activating them all.
- Fixed: A .zip bundle is read in blocks against its real size (an entry that says it is small but inflates to more is refused, and no entry is loaded whole in memory), and needs PHP's ZipArchive; "Run import" only runs for a bundle plugin active on the site; the Playground landing page only opens a path of the exported site; uninstall also removes the note of imported widgets.
- Fixed: Importing a file made elsewhere is safer for users who may not post unfiltered HTML (a site admin on a network): templates, template parts and widgets from the file go through the same HTML filter as other content, custom CSS needs the right to edit CSS, Advanced Custom Fields items need ACF's own capability and never bring PHP callbacks, an existing page keeps its Elementor design unless the import updates existing items, and a malformed source address in the file never rewrites links.

---

## Introduction

> What Eizport does, how it fits into WordPress's own export and import, and where to go next.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/getting-started/introduction/

Eizport moves WordPress content between sites **with everything that makes it work**: the media files, the settings that point to the content, and each post's content as a readable file. It builds on the tools WordPress already has — **Tools → Export** and the **WordPress Importer** — instead of replacing them.

*Screenshot: The Export screen: content types, Product reviews, Attachments and Options in one list, with the file's Details above it.*

### What changes

| WordPress alone | With Eizport |
| --- | --- |
| One content type, or everything | Several types at once, each whole or **by items** — and what they use comes up as a **suggestion** (the products a page shows, the settings that point to it, product reviews) |
| A WXR file (`.xml`) that points to media on the old site | A **bundle** (`.wxrz` or `.zip`) with the media files inside |
| The importer downloads every image from the old site | Media comes from the bundle: the old site can be offline |
| Settings stay behind | **Options** go along: the ones that point to the items (homepage, shop…) are suggested and mapped to the new IDs; add any other one by one |
| Content inside XML | Each post's content as `post_content/<slug>.html` |
| — | A **WordPress Playground** `.zip` that boots a site with the content, theme and plugins |
| — | **As plugin**: a plugin `.zip` that imports itself on the other site with one click ([as plugin](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/as-plugin/)) |
| The importer's own look | **Tools → Import** opens the WordPress Importer directly, dressed like the Export screen |
| — | Every step as an **ability** (Abilities API, REST, MCP) and a **WP-CLI** command |

### Not a full migration — on purpose

Eizport **doesn't copy the whole database**, and that is the point:

- **A full-site migration** (a database dump, a migration plugin) moves everything: transients, logs, sessions, spam, the tables of plugins removed years ago, users, the old site's URLs — and overwrites the site it lands on. Cleaning up afterwards is the hidden cost.
- **WordPress's export** is clean but leaves gaps: the media files stay on the old site (the importer must download them, so it must be online), settings don't travel at all, the homepage stops being the homepage, and images used in content without being attached are left behind.

The plugin takes **what you choose and everything it depends on**: the items, their media files, the media their content uses, the settings that point to them (with IDs remapped on import) and the settings you pick — and **merges** them into the target site. Site URLs, users, keys, roles, active plugins, transients and caches never go.

Use a full migration to clone or move a whole site to new hosting. Use Eizport to move **content**: a section, a store's catalog, a set of pages, a homepage with its settings, a demo.

### How it fits

```text
Tools → Export ──► eizport/export ──► .wxrz / .zip / .xml / Playground .zip
                                          │
Tools → Import → WordPress ◄──────────────┘  (or eizport/import, or wp eizport import)
```

- **Exporting** happens on the new Export screen (or the classic one, if you prefer) and through the `eizport/export` ability. Both run the same code: `export_wp()` with a narrowed query, plus the bundle around it.
- **Importing** uses the WordPress Importer — or the file exported [as plugin](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/as-plugin/) runs it with one click. The plugin unpacks the bundle first, answers the importer's media downloads from it, puts the `.html` contents back into the WXR, and sets the options when the import ends.

### Requirements

- WordPress **7.0** or later (the Export and Settings screens use WordPress's admin screen framework).
- PHP **7.4** or later, with `zlib` (for `.wxrz`) and `ZipArchive` or core's PclZip (for `.zip`).
- The **WordPress Importer** plugin to import (WordPress offers to install it from Tools → Import).

### Next

- [Install the plugin](https://eizport.github.io/docs/getting-started/installation/) and [make your first export](https://eizport.github.io/docs/getting-started/your-first-export/).
- Learn the [Export screen](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/export-screen/), or go straight to the [file formats](https://eizport.github.io/docs/formats/wxrz-bundle/) and the [abilities](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/abilities/).


---

## Installation

> Install the plugin from the WordPress.org plugin directory, check the requirements, and add the WordPress Importer for imports.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/getting-started/installation/

### From the plugin directory

1. In WordPress, go to **Plugins → Add Plugin** and search for **Eizport** — or open its page, [wordpress.org/plugins/eizport](https://wordpress.org/plugins/eizport/).
2. Click **Install Now**, then **Activate**. Tools → Export now opens the new Export screen.

Updates come the same way, from **Dashboard → Updates**.

### With WP-CLI

```bash
wp plugin install eizport --activate
```

### Development versions and older releases

Every release is also on [GitHub](https://github.com/eizport/eizport/releases), as `eizport.zip`: add it in **Plugins → Add Plugin → Upload Plugin**.

### Try it first

Open the [live demo in WordPress Playground](https://playground.wordpress.net/?blueprint-url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eizport/eizport/trunk/playground/blueprint.json): a throwaway site in your browser with the plugin and sample pages.

### To import

Importing needs the **WordPress Importer**. On **Tools → Import**, click **Install Now** under *WordPress*, then **Run Importer**. Exporting works without it.

### Requirements in detail

| Requirement | Why |
| --- | --- |
| WordPress 7.0+ | The Export and Settings screens are built with `@wordpress/build` and booted by core's `@wordpress/boot`. |
| PHP 7.4+ | The plugin's minimum. |
| `zlib` | `.wxrz` bundles are gzipped tar archives. |
| `ZipArchive` (or PclZip) | `.zip` bundles and Playground `.zip` files. Core's PclZip is the fallback. |
| Abilities API | Part of WordPress 6.9+; the screens run the plugin's abilities. |

### Uninstalling

Deleting the plugin removes `wp-content/uploads/eizport/` (temporary copies and unfinished imports), its settings and the saved export defaults (the site's and every user's).


---

## Your first export

> Export a page with its media and the homepage setting, in under a minute.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/getting-started/your-first-export/

This walk-through exports one page — say, the homepage — with its images and the settings that make it the homepage, then imports it on another site.

### 1. Open Tools → Export

The Export screen lists what can be exported: each content type (Posts, Pages, Products…), **Attachments** and **Options**. Nothing is checked yet, which means *everything*.

### 2. Choose the page

Click **Pages** (or *Choose items* in its row). A side panel lists the pages with a checkbox each. Check the homepage — it shows a **Homepage** badge: the Pages row says **1 item** at once. Click **Close**.

*Screenshot: The items panel: pages with their roles as badges (Homepage, Shop page…), the homepage checked.*

The **Options** row now says **2 suggested**: `page_on_front` and `show_on_front` point to the page you chose ([linked settings](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/options/#linked-settings)). Check the row and they come along — it still says *2 suggested*. If the homepage shows products with a WooCommerce block, the **Products** row suggests them the same way.

### 3. Check the file

The **Details** line above the list sums up the file — *WXRZ · default filename · media files*. Click it to open its settings:

- **Format** reads **WXRZ**: a bundle, because media files and settings go with it.
- **Media files** is on: the page's attached images, its featured image and the images in its content go inside.
- **File name** is empty: the file gets WordPress's usual name, shown as the placeholder.

### 4. Export

Click **Export**. The file is written as a [copy](https://eizport.github.io/docs/settings/copies/) on the site and a notice offers **Download**.

### 5. Import it

On the other site, go to **Tools → Import** — it opens the WordPress Importer — upload the `.wxrz` and run the importer as usual. Or export with **As plugin** on, install that `.zip` as a plugin and click **Run import** on its screen ([as plugin](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/as-plugin/)). The page, its images and the homepage setting arrive together — with the new page's ID in `page_on_front`.

> The old site doesn't need to be online: the images come from the bundle.


---

## Importing

> How a bundle is imported with the WordPress Importer, what happens to media, content files and options, and the other ways to import.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/getting-started/importing/

### With the WordPress Importer

Upload a `.wxrz` or `.zip` bundle on **Tools → Import → WordPress**, like any WXR file. Gzipped WXR files (`.xml.gz`) and plain `.xml` files work too.

Exported [as plugin](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/as-plugin/)? Install the `.zip` in **Plugins → Add Plugin → Upload Plugin** and click **Run import** on its row on the Plugins screen instead.

**Tools → Import** opens the WordPress Importer directly, and its screen links to **All importers** ([Settings → General](https://eizport.github.io/docs/settings/general/) turns this off).

The importer looks like the plugin's Export screen: a header with the step's main button (*Upload file and import*, *Submit*), each step in cards, and a **Choose file** button in the admin's language, on the line under its label; *Upload file and import* waits until a file is chosen. **Style Tools → Import → WordPress** in the plugin's [Settings → General](https://eizport.github.io/docs/settings/general/) turns that off; bundles are accepted either way.

### Updating items that already exist

The WordPress Importer skips an item that already exists, and adds a copy when only the slug matches: a theme's *Home* page becomes `home-2`, and a second delivery of the same bundle changes nothing. **Update the items that already exist (same type and slug) instead of adding copies: Pages and Posts** — it names the content types the file holds, and isn't shown when it holds none — on the importer's step 1 (and on the screen of a plugin exported [as plugin](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/as-plugin/)), changes that:

- an item of the same type and slug is **the** item: it gets the bundle's title, content, excerpt, order, custom fields and terms, and keeps its ID;
- settings that point to it (the homepage, the shop page…) point to it, so the theme's *Home* becomes the homepage with the bundle's content;
- attachments that already exist are reused, and their URLs in the updated content point to this site.

It's off unless the bundle asks for it: **Update existing**, in the Export screen's **Details** panel, saves the choice in the bundle, and the box comes checked. The person importing can still uncheck it.

### Versions

- **A bundle made by a newer Eizport** — one that needs a version this site doesn't have — isn't imported: the upload, `wp eizport import`, the ability and a bundle plugin's screen say which Eizport it needs, and the bundle plugin offers **Update now**. Bundles made by older versions import as they did.
- **The WordPress Importer** must be 0.9.6 or newer (Eizport stops and asks to update it). A version newer than the one Eizport was tested with still imports, with a notice on the importer's screen, on the bundle plugin's and in WP-CLI.

### Behind the scenes

Before the importer reads anything:

1. **The bundle is unpacked** into a private folder under `wp-content/uploads/eizport/tmp/<random>/`. Only the files its manifest lists are written, only under that folder, and only with file types WordPress allows to be uploaded (never PHP).
2. **The WXR replaces the upload**, so the importer's own checks and steps run as usual.
3. **Content files go back in:** each `post_content/<slug>.html` is put back into its item, by original ID, else by slug.
4. **Media is served from the bundle:** when the importer downloads an attachment, a `pre_http_request` filter answers with the file from the folder instead of the network.
5. **Options are applied at the end** (`import_end`), with every post ID mapped to the imported post. Options pointing to items that weren't imported are left out.
6. **Term images are mapped at the end:** term meta that hold an attachment ID (a product category's thumbnail), listed in the manifest's `term_media`, point to the imported attachment.

The folder is deleted when the import ends or is abandoned.

### From a copy on the site

Copies made by the Export screen are listed in the plugin's **Settings → Copies** (from its row in Plugins). Each one has an **Import** action, which imports it into the same site — handy to restore content or to test a bundle.

### With code

- The [`eizport/import`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/abilities/#eizportimport) ability imports a `copy` or an `attachment_id` (a `.wxrz`, `.zip` or `.xml` in the media library).
- [`wp eizport import <file>`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/wp-cli/) does it from the command line — also from a bundle folder written by `wp eizport export --dir`, and with `--update-existing`.

### What is mapped

| In the file | On import |
| --- | --- |
| Attachment URLs | Files come from the bundle; the importer creates the attachments and image sizes as usual. An attachment the site already has is reused, with or without *Update existing*: its URLs (and its image sizes') in the imported content point to the file here |
| `post_content/<slug>.html` | Put back into the item's content |
| `options.json` | Set at the end; options listed in `post_ids` get the imported post's ID |
| An edited image's original (`_wp_attachment_edit_root_id`) | Points to the imported original when both come in the bundle; otherwise left out, as the WordPress Importer 0.9.7 does |
| `term_media` in the manifest | Term meta holding an attachment ID get the imported attachment's ID |
| Post IDs in blocks | Image, Gallery, Cover, Media & Text, File, Video and Audio blocks (`"id"`, `"ids"`, `"mediaId"`, `wp-image-N`, gallery `data-id`), `[gallery ids]` and navigation links to pages and posts point to the imported items, in new and updated items and in block widgets. Plugins add their blocks with `eizport_block_id_attributes` |
| The look ([appearance](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/appearance/)) | CSS rules added to this site's CSS as the bundle asks (end or start; head/tail comments), or — chosen on import — replacing a head/tail block of the same name or all the CSS — step 1 of the importer, `css_mode`/`css_markers` and `--css-mode`/`--[no-]css-markers` change it; theme mods, style groups and widgets join this site's |
| Terms | The items' categories, tags and other terms come in full (description, parent, term meta) and are created parents first; a term the site already has (same slug) is used as it is |
| Links to the source site | The source site's address (the WXR's `base_site_url`) becomes this site's in the imported items' content and excerpt (also escaped in block attributes, http or https), in the menus' custom links, and in widgets and theme mods |
| Products and their variations, pages and their children | Imported with their parents, as the WordPress Importer does |


---

## Multisite

> Eizport on a WordPress network: network or per-site activation, who can do what, where each site's files go, WP-CLI with --url, and uninstalling.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/getting-started/multisite/

Eizport works on each site of a network as on a single site: a site exports its own content and imports into itself, whatever the other sites hold.

### Activating

**Network Activate** it in *Network Admin → Plugins* to have it on every site, or activate it on the sites that need it. Nothing is shared between sites: each keeps its own settings, copies and saved defaults.

### Who can do what

| Who | Can |
| --- | --- |
| Site administrators | Export and import on their site, and change its Eizport settings. A [Playground .zip](https://eizport.github.io/docs/formats/playground-zip/) takes only the plugins active on their site and the themes it may use — no must-use plugins: the network's code is the super admins'. On import, the bundle's options outside the [groups](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/options/#options-outside-the-groups-on-import) and the custom CSS aren't set |
| Super admins | All of that on every site, and install plugins — an [as plugin](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/as-plugin/) `.zip` needs one to install it; site administrators import the bundle inside it on Tools → Import instead |
| Users who can't post unfiltered HTML | Import as WordPress lets them: on a network only super admins can, so scripts and some embeds in imported content — templates, template parts and widgets too — are filtered for the others, as they would be when typed in the editor |

### Each site's files

A site's media, copies (`uploads/eizport/`) and imported files live in its own uploads folder (`wp-content/uploads/sites/<id>/`). An export from one site and an import into another — subsite to subsite, a subsite to a single site, or the reverse — work as between two separate sites:

- the media come from the bundle into the importing site's folder;
- links to the exporting site (its own address, like `https://example.com/shop`) point to the importing one;
- the IDs in blocks, menus and settings point to the imported items.

### Saved defaults

*Save as default* keeps each user's choices **per site**: what someone saves on one site doesn't show on another. With *Defaults are saved for: The whole site* in the [general settings](https://eizport.github.io/docs/settings/general/), a site has its own defaults for everyone on it.

### WP-CLI

Pick the site with `--url`:

```bash
wp --url=https://example.com/shop eizport export --types=product --filename=shop
wp --url=https://example.com/staging eizport import shop.wxrz
```

### Uninstalling

Deleting the plugin from *Network Admin → Plugins* removes its data from every site of the network: each site's `uploads/eizport/` folder, settings, saved defaults and scheduled cleanup.


---

## Header menus to staging

> A site built locally — pages, a header menu with submenus and its theme location — repeated on staging without rebuilding the menu by hand.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/use-cases/header-menus-to-staging/

### The scenario

A site is built locally from a design: the pages, then the header menu — *Home*, *About*, *Services* with three pages under it, *Contact* and a link to the shop — set in the theme's *Primary* location. Staging needs the same pages and the same menu, and nobody wants to rebuild the menu by hand, item by item, after every round of changes.

### The steps

1. On the local site, **Tools → Export**. Check **Pages** — or only the ones the menu links to.
2. The **Menus** row says *1 suggested*: the menu in the *Primary* location. Check it. Opening its panel shows it as a *Classic menu* in *Primary*.
3. If a page of the menu wasn't chosen, the **Pages** row suggests it: check the row to bring it.
4. **Export**, and on staging **Tools → Import → WordPress** with the file (Eizport active there too, for the menu's location).

The same works for a block theme's header: the **Menus** row suggests the *Navigation* the header uses.

### What the file carries

- The pages, with their media.
- The menu, with its items in order, the submenu under *Services*, the custom link to the shop, and its place in *Primary*.

On staging, the menu items point to staging's pages (their new IDs) and the menu is in *Primary*.

### What it doesn't

- A page the menu links to that wasn't exported: its item is left out.
- The location, when staging's theme doesn't have *Primary* (another theme, or a block theme).

### Next time

After more changes, export again and import with *Update the items that already exist (same type and slug)* checked (see [updating items that already exist](https://eizport.github.io/docs/getting-started/importing/#updating-items-that-already-exist)): the pages are updated, and the menu takes the file's items instead of getting a second copy of them.


---

## Theme look to staging

> A change to a theme's look made locally — the last CSS rule, the logo, one widget, or a block theme's palette — taken to staging without touching what staging has of its own.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/use-cases/theme-look-to-staging/

### The scenario

Staging already has its look: its own Additional CSS, its widgets, its colors. Locally, a last CSS rule was added for the footer, the logo changed, and an *Hours* widget went into the footer. Only those should reach staging — copying the whole look over would wipe what staging has of its own, and redoing it by hand is where something gets forgotten.

The same goes for a block theme customized in the Site Editor: a new color palette, one more rule in its Additional CSS.

### The steps

1. On the local site, **Tools → Export**. Open **Choose items** on **Customizer custom CSS** and check only the last rule (*Rule 3 of 3 (the last)*), each with its preview; on **Customizer theme mods**, the Logo; on **Widgets**, *Hours*. With a block theme: the *Color palette* group of **Editor global styles** and a rule of **Editor global CSS**.
2. **Details → CSS rules on import**: *Add at the end of the site's CSS* (the default).
3. **Export**, and on staging **Tools → Import → WordPress** with the file (with Eizport active there). Step 1 shows **Additional CSS**, as the file asks; change it there if needed.

### What staging gets

- Its own CSS, then the rule, between `/* head … */` and `/* tail … */` comments named after the file.
- The logo (the image is imported with it); its other theme mods as they were.
- *Hours* at the end of its footer, after its own widgets.
- With a block theme: the palette; its own colors and typography as they were.

### Next time

Name the exports after the task — `COMB-584.wxrz` — and the rules on staging sit between `/* head COMB-584 */` and `/* tail COMB-584 */`. Another change for the same task, another export with the same name — with **Details → CSS rules on import: Replace the block of the same name**: the importer's step 1 comes with **Replace the "COMB-584" block this site already has** chosen, which swaps the old rules for the new ones and leaves the rest of staging's CSS as it is. With *Add at the end* instead, a second block is added after the first (the importer offers the replacement too). With *Update existing* on, the *Hours* widget is updated in place instead of added again.

### What it doesn't

- Fonts installed with the Font Library.
- A sidebar staging's theme doesn't have: its widgets go to *Inactive widgets*.


---

## Site header to staging

> A block theme's header redone in the Site Editor locally — a new layout, its navigation, an image — and a page template, taken to staging in place of the ones staging has, without a Header 2.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/use-cases/site-header-to-staging/

### The scenario

The site uses a block theme. Locally, the header was redone in **Appearance → Editor**: the logo on the left, a new navigation, a banner image above it; and the **Pages** template got a line of its own above the content. Staging has its own header, edited there months ago.

Copying the block markup by hand loses the navigation (its `ref` is an ID of the local site) and the image (another ID), and the WordPress Importer alone adds the header again as *Header 2* next to staging's own, which keeps showing.

### The steps

1. On the local site, **Tools → Export**. Check **Editor template parts** — or open **Choose items** and check only **Header**, each part with its block markup as preview — and **Editor templates** (**Pages**).
2. Check **Menus** too, with the header's navigation: it's suggested, as the templates point to it.
3. **Export**, and on staging **Tools → Import → WordPress** with the file (with Eizport active there).

### What staging gets

- Its **Header** replaced by the local one, under the same slug — no *Header 2* — and the **Pages** template replaced (or added, when staging hadn't edited it).
- The header's navigation block pointing to the imported navigation, its image block to the imported image, and its links to the local site pointing to staging.
- Everything else of staging's look as it was: its other templates and parts, its styles, its CSS.

### What it doesn't

- Templates the theme's files hold and nobody edited: staging's theme has them already.
- Another theme's templates: only the active theme's are listed, and they go to the same theme on staging. With another theme active there, they wait until that theme is.


---

## Galleries to staging

> Pages built with Image, Gallery and Cover blocks, moved to a site where the media get other IDs — and still editable as they were.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/use-cases/galleries-to-staging/

### The scenario

The local site's pages use Image, Gallery, Cover and Media & Text blocks. Staging already has content, so the imported images get other IDs there. With the WordPress Importer alone, the images still show (their addresses are updated), but the blocks keep the old IDs: the editor shows *This image has an empty or invalid source*, *Replace* and the image settings act on the wrong item, and a gallery can't find its images.

### The steps

1. On the local site, **Tools → Export**: check the pages. Their images come along (*media used in content*).
2. **Export**, and on staging **Tools → Import → WordPress** with the file.

### What the import does

When the import ends, every imported page — new or updated — has its blocks pointed to the imported media: the Image and Cover blocks' `id` and `wp-image-N` class, the Gallery's `ids` and its images' `data-id`, Media & Text's `mediaId`, File, Video and Audio, `[gallery ids="…"]`, and the navigation links to pages and posts. The same goes for block widgets.

Only IDs that came in the file and changed are touched: a block pointing to something staging already had, and that wasn't in the file, stays as it is.

### What it doesn't

- A plugin's own blocks, until it lists them (the [`eizport_block_id_attributes`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/hooks/#eizport_block_id_attributes) filter).


---

## Internal links to staging

> Pages that link to each other, to products and to categories, built locally and moved to staging — with every link pointing to staging, not back to the local site.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/use-cases/internal-links-to-staging/

### The scenario

The local site's home links to the shop, to three product categories, to the *About* page and to a few products — in buttons, in navigation links, in the text. With the WordPress Importer alone, staging gets those links as they were: `http://localhost:8909/product/…`, so every click on staging leads back to a site only one computer can open. The fix used to be a `search-replace` after each import.

### The steps

1. On the local site, **Tools → Export**: check the pages and products (and the menus, the widgets…).
2. **Export**, and on staging **Tools → Import → WordPress** with the file.

### What the import does

When the import ends, the local site's address becomes staging's in what was imported:

- the content and excerpt of every imported item, new or updated — links in the text, buttons, navigation links (also inside block attributes, where the address is escaped as `http:\/\/…`), with http or https;
- the custom links of the imported classic menus;
- the widgets and theme mods that came in the file.

The address is replaced only where it ends: `old.example` never touches `old.example.org`.

### What it doesn't

- Content that wasn't in the file: staging's own pages keep their links.
- Templates and template parts aren't exported yet, so links in a block theme's header or footer stay as they were.


---

## Product categories to staging

> A store's products moved with their categories as they are — descriptions, parent categories and thumbnails — not just their names.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/use-cases/product-categories-to-staging/

### The scenario

The local store has its products in categories with descriptions (shown on the category pages), some under a parent (*Coffee → Single origin*), and with thumbnails. Only the products are exported, not *All content*. With WordPress's own export, each product names its categories and nothing else: staging gets categories with the right names and no description, no parent, no thumbnail.

### The steps

1. On the local site, **Tools → Export**: check **Products** (all of them, or some).
2. **Export**, and on staging **Tools → Import → WordPress** with the file.

### What the file carries

Every category, tag and other term the exported items use, in full, with its parent categories even when no product is in them:

- the name, the slug and the **description**;
- the **parent**, so the hierarchy is rebuilt (parents are written first);
- the **term meta**: WooCommerce's thumbnail and display type, or a plugin's own fields.

On staging, the categories come as they were, and the thumbnails point to the imported images.

### What it doesn't

- A category staging already has (same slug) is used as it is: its description isn't overwritten.
- Terms no exported item uses stay out — export *All content* to bring every term.


---

## Second delivery to staging

> Delivering new pages to a staging site that already has the media from the first delivery — without duplicating the images and without links to the local site.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/use-cases/second-delivery-to-staging/

### The scenario

The first delivery to staging brought the pages and their images. A week later there are two new pages that reuse some of those images, plus one new image. The second export carries them all; staging already has most of the images.

### The steps

1. On the local site, **Tools → Export**: check the two new pages (their images come along).
2. **Export**, and on staging **Tools → Import → WordPress** with the file — *Update existing* on or off.

### What the import does

- The images staging already has (same title and date as in the file) are **reused**, not imported again.
- Their addresses in the new pages — the full size and every image size (`photo-300x200.jpg`) — point to the files on staging, not to the local site. Before, this only happened with *Update existing* on.
- The new image is imported, and the blocks point to it ([galleries to staging](https://eizport.github.io/docs/use-cases/galleries-to-staging/)).

### What it doesn't

- An image whose file changed locally keeps staging's old file: turn on *Update existing* to update pages, and replace the image in the media library.


---

## Subsite to subsite

> On a network, a site built in one subsite moved to another — the live one, or a fresh copy — with its media, links and settings pointing to the right site.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/use-cases/subsite-to-subsite/

### The scenario

A network has a subsite for building (`example.com/build`) and the live one (`example.com/shop`). The new pages, products and menus are ready in *build*; *shop* needs them. Copying the database tables between subsites is risky (IDs, prefixes, users shared by the network), and WordPress's own export leaves links and images pointing to *build*.

### The steps

1. In *build*, **Tools → Export**: check what goes (pages, products, menus, the look…).
2. **Export**, and in *shop* **Tools → Import → WordPress** with the file. Or from WP-CLI:

   ```bash
   wp --url=https://example.com/build eizport export --types=page,product --menus=all --filename=release
   wp --url=https://example.com/shop eizport import release.wxrz --update-existing
   ```

### What the import does

- The media go to *shop*'s own folder (`uploads/sites/<id>/`).
- Links to `example.com/build/…` point to `example.com/shop/…`; the network's address and *shop*'s own uploads are never touched.
- The IDs in blocks, menus and settings point to the items imported into *shop*.
- *build*'s saved defaults and settings stay in *build*.

### What it doesn't

- Users: they belong to the network; the importer assigns the posts to an existing user (or creates one) as WordPress does.
- Network settings (*Network Admin → Settings*) aren't exported: they belong to the whole network.


---

## Client demo in Playground

> A new page shown to a client in WordPress Playground: one link that opens right on that page, with the site's plugins as they are.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/use-cases/client-demo-in-playground/

### The scenario

A new landing page is ready locally and the client wants to see it before it goes to staging. Sending a link to a local site doesn't work, and a Playground that opens on the dashboard, with every plugin switched on (including the ones the site keeps off), isn't what the client should see.

### The steps

1. On the local site, **Tools → Export**: check the page (and what it needs: menus, the look…).
2. **Details → Format: Playground**, then **Playground options**:
   - **Landing page → A page**: the new landing page;
   - **Themes and plugins**: the site's theme and the plugins the page uses.
3. **Export**, then **Open in Playground** on the copy in the plugin's [Copies](https://eizport.github.io/docs/settings/copies/): that's the link to send, on playground.wordpress.net.

### What the client sees

Playground builds the site in the browser and opens **on the landing page** — the page goes in the blueprint as `/?pagename=<its path>`, so it's found whatever ID it gets there. The plugins are on or off as they are locally: a plugin the site keeps inactive is installed but stays off.

### What it doesn't

- The link opens a throwaway site: what the client changes there is lost when the tab closes.
- Premium plugins go inside the file: share it only where their licenses allow.


---

## Playground in your language

> A demo of an English site shown in Portuguese in WordPress Playground: the dashboard, the theme and the plugins translated, from one link.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/use-cases/playground-in-your-language/

### The scenario

The site is built in English, but the client is Brazilian and wants to see the new page and its admin in Portuguese. A Playground link opens in English, and switching the language there means downloading translations by hand on a throwaway site.

### The steps

1. In **Users → Profile**, your language is *Português do Brasil* (the site's stays English).
2. **Tools → Export**: check the page and what it needs.
3. **Details → Format: Playground**, then **Playground options**:
   - **Language → Your language (Português do Brasil)**;
   - **Themes and plugins**: the site's theme and the plugins the page uses.
4. **Export**, then **Open in Playground** on the copy in [Copies](https://eizport.github.io/docs/settings/copies/).

### What the client sees

Playground installs the themes and plugins, then sets the site's language to Portuguese and fetches the translations of WordPress and of everything from the WordPress.org directory. A custom plugin's translations come from this site, inside the file. The dashboard, the theme's texts and the plugins' screens open in Portuguese.

### What it doesn't

- Only languages installed on this site are offered (Settings → General or your profile installs them).
- A theme or plugin without a translation stays in English.


---

## Custom post types in Playground

> A site whose post types live in a must-use plugin, shown in WordPress Playground: the plugin goes in the .zip and runs before the import.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/use-cases/custom-post-types-in-playground/

### The scenario

The site keeps its **Recipes** post type in a must-use plugin — `wp-content/mu-plugins/recipes.php`, which loads `recipes/register.php` — so no one can switch it off. A Playground demo with the recipes needs that plugin: without it, there's no Recipes post type to import into.

### The steps

1. **Tools → Export**: check **Recipes** (and what the recipes need).
2. **Details → Format: Playground**, then **Playground options → Themes and plugins**:
   - **Must-use plugins to install**: the recipes plugin;
   - the site's theme, and the plugins the recipes use.
3. **Export**, then **Open in Playground** on the copy in [Copies](https://eizport.github.io/docs/settings/copies/).

### What happens

The `.zip` holds `mu-plugins/recipes.php` and `mu-plugins/recipes.zip` (the folder it loads). The blueprint writes them into Playground's `wp-content/mu-plugins/` **before the import**, so the Recipes post type exists when the recipes come in, and the menu shows **Recipes** with them.

### What it doesn't

- A host's own must-use plugins (and WordPress Studio's SQLite loader) aren't offered: Playground has its own.
- A must-use plugin that loads files from elsewhere (a path outside `mu-plugins/`) takes only what's in `mu-plugins/`.
- Custom code goes inside the file: share it only where its license allows.


---

## Advanced Custom Fields to staging

> Recipes built with Advanced Custom Fields (ACF) — their post type, taxonomy, field group and values — taken to staging with every photo, page and term they point to pointing right.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/use-cases/advanced-custom-fields-to-staging/

### The scenario

A food site keeps its **Recipes** with Advanced Custom Fields (ACF): a *Recipes* post type and a *Cuisines* taxonomy made in *ACF → Post Types* and *Taxonomies*, and a *Recipe details* field group with a photo, a printable card, the chef's page, related pages, a cuisine and the cook. A new recipe is ready locally; staging has its own content, so every ID there is different.

### The steps

1. On the local site, **Tools → Export**: check **Recipes** (or open **Choose items** for the new one).
2. The rows suggest the rest: **Pages** shows *2 suggested* (the chef's page and the related one) and **Advanced Custom Fields (ACF)** shows *3 suggested* (the post type, the taxonomy and the field group). Check both rows.
3. **Export** (a `.wxrz` or `.zip` bundle), and import it on staging in **Tools → Import → WordPress**.

### What staging gets

- ACF imports the *Recipes* post type, the *Cuisines* taxonomy and the *Recipe details* group **before** the content: the recipe comes in as a recipe, with its cuisine.
- The photo and the card come with the bundle, even unattached; on staging they keep their place — or point to the same files staging already had.
- The chef's page, the related pages, the cuisine and the cook point to the items **there**, with staging's IDs; the group's location rule on a page too.
- A second delivery updates the group, the post type and the taxonomy (same keys) instead of adding copies.

### What it doesn't

- ACF PRO fields (repeater, flexible content, gallery) aren't covered yet.
- A cook who isn't an author in the file keeps the old user ID; authors are mapped as the importer maps them.


---

## Elementor to staging

> A landing page built with Elementor — its images, a saved section template and the site's global colors and fonts — taken to staging with Elementor's own importer, everything pointing to staging's items.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/use-cases/elementor-to-staging/

### The scenario

A landing page is built with Elementor locally: a background image, a gallery, a **promo section saved as a template** and shown by a template widget, a button to the chef's page, and the brand color and font from *Elementor → Site Settings*. Staging already has its own content, so every ID there is different, and its own Kit.

### The steps

1. On the local site, **Tools → Export**: in **Pages**, **Choose items** → the landing page.
2. The **Elementor** row shows *2 suggested*: the site settings and the promo section. Check it.
3. **Export**: the page's design goes as `post_content/<slug>.json`, the template and the site settings in the bundle, with the images.
4. On staging, **Tools → Import → WordPress**: upload the bundle.

### What staging gets

- The page, with its design brought in by **Elementor's own import**: the background and the gallery show the images the bundle brought (no copies of them), the template widget shows the imported promo section, and the button goes to staging's chef page.
- The **promo section** in *Templates → Saved Templates*.
- A **Kit** with the brand color and font added to staging's, active — the heading shows the brand color.
- A second delivery updates the template and that Kit instead of adding copies.

### What it doesn't

- Elementor Pro's Theme Builder (headers, footers and their conditions) and popups aren't covered yet.


---

## Export screen

> The new Tools → Export screen, part by part: the header actions, the Details panel, the list and the side panels.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/export-screen/

Tools → Export opens a screen built like WordPress's newest admin screens (DataViews and DataForm, on core's admin screen framework). It runs the plugin's [abilities](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/abilities/), so the screen, REST and AI agents export the same way.

*Screenshot: The Export screen with Pages (1 item), and Products and Options bringing what the homepage suggests.*

### The list

One row per thing that can be exported:

- **Content types** — Posts, Pages, Products, Orders, Coupons, Forms and any custom post type with an admin screen. Children travel with their parents (a product's variations).
- **Attachments** — media items, chosen directly.
- **Product reviews** — WooCommerce's approved reviews, right after Products ([choosing items](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/choosing-items/#suggestions)). Products go without their reviews unless this row is checked.
- **Options** — site settings ([more](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/options/)).

The **Export** column says what goes: *Not included*, *All*, *3 items*, or for Options *Basics + 2 items*; an unchecked Options row shows *2 suggested* (the homepage: `page_on_front` and `show_on_front`) when the items chosen have [linked settings](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/options/#linked-settings). **Nothing checked exports all content**, as WordPress does.

Each row's actions: **Choose items** (opens the side panel; always shown, not only on hover; **Close items** on the row whose panel is open), **Export all of it** (where it doesn't export all yet; for Options, every option) and **Leave out** (rows included). Check several rows to act on them at once.

### The side panel

Clicking a row opens its items in a panel on the right ([choosing items](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/choosing-items/)): what you check there joins the export at once, and **Close** goes back. The panel's URL is shareable: `…&p=/export?type=page`.

### The Details panel

Above the list, a **Details** line sums up the file — like *WXRZ · default filename · media files · as plugin* (*custom filename* once you type one). Click it to open its settings (it always starts closed):

| Field | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Format** | *WXR XML* (WordPress's plain file), *WXRZ* or *WXR ZIP* (a bundle, as soon as media files or settings go with it) or *Playground* ([formats](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/file-and-formats/)) |
| **File name** | Empty: WordPress's usual `<site>.WordPress.<date>`, shown as the placeholder |
| **Media files** | Put the exported attachments' files inside the bundle; its ⓘ explains it |
| **As plugin** | Make the bundle a plugin that imports itself ([as plugin](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/as-plugin/)); its ⓘ explains it. Off and disabled with Playground |
| **Update existing** | The import updates the items of the chosen content types that already exist (same type and slug) instead of adding copies, named in its ⓘ (all with nothing checked); disabled when only rows without content are checked ([more](https://eizport.github.io/docs/getting-started/importing/#updating-items-that-already-exist)); its ⓘ explains it. Off and disabled with Playground, which starts from a new site |
| **Playground options** | Where the Playground .zip opens and the themes and plugins it installs (enabled with the Playground format); a count on the button says how many are set ([Playground .zip](https://eizport.github.io/docs/formats/playground-zip/#playground-options)) |

### Header actions

- **Reset to defaults** — goes back to the saved defaults (or to nothing chosen, without them). Dimmed when the choices already are those.
- **Clear defaults** — forgets the saved defaults; active only while **Reset to defaults** is dimmed.
- **Save as default** — keeps the current choices to start with next time ([saved defaults](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/saved-defaults/)).
- **Export** — writes the file as a [copy](https://eizport.github.io/docs/settings/copies/) and offers the download.

### On a phone

The list shows only the title column, with what is exported under it; the Details panel stacks; the side panel takes the screen.


---

## Choosing items

> Items per content type, chosen in the side panel at once; suggestions; the Selection filter; children, attachments, reviews and roles.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/choosing-items/

Each content type is exported whole (its row checked in the list) or **by items**, chosen in its side panel.

*Screenshot: The Pages panel: a checkbox per page, roles as badges.*

### Choosing

Check an item, or click it, and it joins the export at once: the list behind the panel shows **1 item**, **3 items**… Uncheck the last one and the type is left out again. The choice survives search and paging: check some on page 1, search, check more. **Close** goes back to the list. The Options panel works the same way.

### Suggestions

What you choose can suggest more, shown as **N suggested** in the other rows — counted, not named, and not exported until that row is checked:

| Choosing | Suggests |
| --- | --- |
| A page a setting points to (homepage, posts page, shop…) | Those settings, in **Options** ([linked settings](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/options/#linked-settings)) |
| A page whose blocks show products (*Hand-picked Products*, *Product Collection* with hand-picked products, *Single Product*, *Featured Product*, `[products ids="…"]`) | Those products, in **Products** |
| Products with reviews | Their approved reviews, in **Product reviews** |
| Anything | The classic menus in the theme's locations and the navigations the items or the theme's templates use, in **Menus** ([menus](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/menus/)) |
| A menu | The pages, posts and products it links to, in their rows |

Checking a row with suggestions brings them, and it still says *2 suggested* — with what else you chose: *2 suggested + Basics + 1 item*. Unchecking one of them in the row's panel turns the rest into plain items. **Export all of it** takes the whole type instead. Plugins add their own suggestions with [`eizport_suggested_items`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/hooks/#eizport_suggested_items).

### Finding items

- **Selection** — *All*, *Selected* or *Suggested*. A panel opens on *Selected* when its row has items chosen, else on *Suggested* when there are suggestions.
- **Status** and each **taxonomy** (product categories, tags…) narrow the list to find items; they don't export anything by themselves.

Exporting by filters (status, author, dates, terms) stays on the [classic screen](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/classic-screen/) and in the [`eizport/export`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/abilities/) ability.

### What comes along

| With | Comes along |
| --- | --- |
| Any item | Its attached media and featured image (WordPress does this) |
| Any item | Media used in its content without being attached ([media](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/media/)) |
| Any item | Its categories, tags and other terms in full — description, parent categories and term meta (a product category's thumbnail and display type) — not only their names |
| A product | Its variations. Its reviews only with the **Product reviews** row (they are suggested) — on the classic screen and in the ability without `reviews`, all of them |
| A page | Its child pages only if they are chosen too |
| An item with a role | The settings that point to it, suggested in the Options row ([linked settings](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/options/#linked-settings)) |

### Roles

Items that a setting points to show a badge: **Homepage**, **Posts page**, **Privacy policy page**, **Site icon**, and the pages plugins register, like WooCommerce's **Shop page**, **Cart page**, **Checkout page**, **My account page** and **Terms and conditions page**. Plugins add their own through [`eizport_linked_options`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/hooks/#eizport_linked_options).

### Limits

The classic screen lists the latest 1,000 items per type (filter [`eizport_selection_limit`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/hooks/#eizport_selection_limit)); the new screen pages through all of them.


---

## Options

> Export site settings one by one, by group or all at once; linked settings; what is never exported; how IDs are mapped.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/options/

The **Options** row exports site settings in an `options.json` inside the bundle, set on the other site when the import ends.

*Screenshot: The Options panel on Selected: the settings the homepage brings.*

### Three ways to choose

- **One by one** — every option the site has (search, pages), each with its size and an *IDs mapped on import* badge when it holds a post ID.
- **By group** — filter the panel by a group and export it: **Basics** (suggested), Reading, General, Permalinks, Discussion, Media, Privacy, Site logo and site icon, WooCommerce pages. The theme's Customizer settings, custom CSS, the Site Editor's styles and the widgets have [rows of their own](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/appearance/). A group is resolved when the file is made, so it follows the active theme.
- **All** — every option that may be exported.

On the new screen, checking an option in the panel adds it at once (the *Selection* filter shows the ones chosen); groups and *all* come from saved defaults or the classic screen. With nothing chosen yet, the panel opens on **Basics**: title, tagline, language, time zone, date formats, homepage and posts page, posts per page, permalinks, site logo and site icon.

### Linked settings

Some options point to a post: `page_on_front`, `page_for_posts`, `wp_page_for_privacy_policy`, `site_icon`, WooCommerce's page IDs. When the post is exported, those options can come along — with the ones they need, like `show_on_front`.

On the new screen they are **suggested**: choose the homepage and the unchecked Options row shows **2 suggested** (`page_on_front` and `show_on_front`, counted, not named). Check the row and they go with the export; the row still says **2 suggested** (plus groups or *N items* you chose). Uncheck one of them in its panel and the rest become plain items — **1 item**. Leave the row unchecked and they don't go.

The setting decides when they are suggested or added:

| Mode (Settings → Export) | When |
| --- | --- |
| **When items are checked, and on export** (default) | Suggested in the Options row when you check an item with a role; on the classic screen and in the ability, also added when the file is made — for items exported by filters or with all content |
| **When items are checked** | Suggested from the side panel's selection |
| **On export** | Only when the file is made (classic screen, ability) |
| **Never** | You choose every option yourself |

### Never exported

Site URLs (`siteurl`, `home`), the admin email, keys and salts, `active_plugins`, roles (`<prefix>user_roles`), who may register and as what (`users_can_register`, `default_role`), `cron`, `rewrite_rules`, database versions, mail server credentials, the plugin's own settings, and every transient. Plugins add theirs with [`eizport_denied_options`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/hooks/#eizport_denied_options); WordPress's own can't be removed.

**Secrets** aren't exported nor listed either: an option, a theme mod or a widget field whose name says it holds one — `secret`, `password`, `token`, `api_key`, `license`, `private`, `credential`… — and plugins' known stores of them (WP Mail SMTP, payment gateways' settings). A plugin marks its own, or lets one through, with [`eizport_is_secret`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/hooks/#eizport_is_secret).

An import never sets WordPress's own either, whatever the bundle holds: a bundle is a file anyone could have written.

### Options outside the groups, on import

An import sets the options of the groups (with the ones plugins add), the options pointing to a post, the theme mods and the widgets. Any other option the bundle holds — exported **by name** — waits for whoever imports: step 1 of the importer lists them under **Other options**, unchecked, and only the ones checked are set (on a [bundle plugin](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/as-plugin/)'s screen too). With [WP-CLI](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/wp-cli/) and the [`eizport/import`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/abilities/#eizportimport) ability, only the ones named in `--options` / `options`. On a network, only for who may manage the network's options.

### IDs on import

`options.json` lists, under `post_ids`, the options that hold a post ID. On import each one gets the ID the importer gave that post; if the post wasn't imported, the option is left out rather than pointing to the wrong thing. `theme_mods_<theme>` values are mapped too (logo, menus).


---

## Menus

> Classic menus with their items and theme locations, and block navigations, on their own row; what's suggested, what the import does with menus the other site already has, and the limits.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/menus/

Navigation menus are exported on their own row, **Menus**, next to the content types. Its side panel lists both kinds:

| Kind | What it is | Goes with it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Classic menu** | *Appearance → Menus*, in classic themes | Its items (with their order and submenus) and the theme locations it sits in |
| **Navigation** | The menu of a *Navigation* block, in block themes (*Appearance → Editor → Navigation*) | Its links |

### Suggested

Without choosing anything, the row suggests:

- the classic menus that sit in a **theme location** (*Primary*, *Footer*…);
- the **navigations** the items chosen use in their content, and the ones the active theme's templates and template parts use (a header's *Navigation* block). A *Navigation* block that points to no menu shows the most recently published one: that one is suggested.

Choosing a classic menu suggests what its items link to — pages, posts, products — in their rows. Export them too: the importer leaves out a menu item whose page isn't on the other site. Custom links always go.

### On the other site

- **Classic menus** are created with their items, which point to the imported pages, posts and terms; submenus keep their parents. Each menu goes back to its **theme locations**, when the other site's active theme has them (a block theme has none). The locations need Eizport on the other site: with the WordPress Importer alone, the menus come without them.
- **Navigations** are created, and the *Navigation* blocks that pointed to them — in the imported pages and in the other site's templates — point to the new ones.
- **A menu the other site already has** (same slug) keeps its items, unless the import [updates the items that already exist](https://eizport.github.io/docs/getting-started/importing/#updating-items-that-already-exist): then its items are replaced by the file's, and it ends up as on this site. A navigation with the same slug is updated the same way.

### From WP-CLI and the ability

```bash
wp eizport export --types=page --menus=classic:18,navigation:4
wp eizport export --menus=all
```

The [`eizport/export`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/abilities/#eizportexport) ability takes `menus` (`classic`, `navigation` or `all`); [`eizport/get-export-options`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/abilities/#eizportget-export-options) lists them.

### Limits

- **All content** (no type chosen) already carries every menu, as WordPress's own export does; choosing menus there adds their theme locations.
- With no type checked and menus chosen, only the menus are exported.
- The classic screen (*Tools → Export → Classic*) has no Menus row.


---

## Appearance

> The site's look on rows of its own, item by item: Customizer theme mods and CSS rules, the Site Editor's style groups, CSS rules, templates and template parts, and widgets — with a preview of each, the media they use, and how the other site takes them.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/appearance/

The site's look is exported on rows of its own, next to the content types. A row shows only when the active theme has something in it, and its **Choose items** panel lists what it holds, each with a preview:

| Row | Each item | Preview | Shows with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Customizer theme mods** | A setting of *Appearance → Customize*: Logo, Header image, Background image and color, Header text color, the theme's own settings | The image, the color, or the value | A theme with Customizer settings |
| **Customizer custom CSS** | A rule of *Customize → Additional CSS* (an `@media` block counts as one; a comment right before goes with it) | The rule, and which one it is: *Rule 3 of 3 (the last)* | A theme with Additional CSS |
| **Editor global styles** | A group of *Appearance → Editor → Styles*: Color palette, Site colors, Typography, Spacing and layout, Elements, each block with styles of its own | Its colors, or a summary | Block themes with saved styles |
| **Editor global CSS** | A rule of the Site Editor's *Additional CSS* | The rule | Block themes with Additional CSS there |
| **Editor templates** | A template of the active theme edited in *Appearance → Editor → Templates* (Pages, Single Posts, a custom one) | Its block markup | Block themes with templates edited there |
| **Editor template parts** | A template part of the active theme edited there: the Header, the Footer, a part of its own, with its area | Its block markup | Block themes with parts edited there |
| **Widgets** | A widget — classic (text, image, menu…) or block — with its sidebar | Its text or image | Classic themes with widgets in their sidebars |

Check a row to take all it has (every item is suggested), or open **Choose items** and check only some: the last CSS rule, the logo and the background color, one widget, the header. They need a bundle (`.wxrz`, `.zip` or a Playground `.zip`): they travel in its `options.json` — but templates and template parts, which are posts and travel in the WXR as content does (a plain `.xml` carries them too).

Only what was edited in the Site Editor is listed: a template the theme's own files hold, untouched, the other site's theme has already.

### What comes along

The images the items chosen use are exported with them, even when the Attachments row isn't checked: the logo, the header and background images, the media of image widgets and block widgets, the images in templates and template parts, and the uploads the styles and the CSS point to (*Only attached media* in [Settings → Export](https://eizport.github.io/docs/settings/export-settings/) turns it off, as for content).

### On the other site

- **CSS rules** (the Customizer's and the Site Editor's) are **added** to the other site's CSS, as **Details → CSS rules on import** says: at the end (the default), at the start, replacing the block of the same name the other site already has (at the end when it has none), or replacing all its CSS. They go between two comments named after the file:

  ```css
  .their-own { color: purple; }

  /* head COMB-584 */
  .site-footer { background: #ffeedd; }
  /* tail COMB-584 */
  ```

  The name is the file's name without extension — `COMB-584.wxrz` here, named after a task: a mark of where the rules came from. Each import adds its own block — blocks aren't unique, and the same name can show up more than once. Without the comments ([Settings → Export](https://eizport.github.io/docs/settings/export-settings/), or the importer), rules the other site already has (same text) aren't repeated.
- Whoever imports starts from the export's choice and can change it on the importer's step 1 (**Additional CSS**), with `css_mode`/`css_markers` in [`eizport/import`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/abilities/#eizportimport), or with `--css-mode`/`--[no-]css-markers` in [WP-CLI](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/wp-cli/). There:
  - **Replace the "COMB-584" block this site already has** — offered only when the other site's CSS has a head/tail block of the same name (an earlier delivery of a file with that name): the new block takes its place, the rest of the CSS staying (`replace`);
  - **Replace all of this site's CSS** — only the file's rules remain (`replace_all`).
- **Theme mods** chosen go to the active theme and are **merged** into its own: what the file doesn't hold stays (the other settings, the menus' locations). The logo and the header image point to the imported attachments, the header and background images' addresses to the imported files.
- **Style groups** chosen replace the same groups on the other site's styles (a block theme); its other groups stay.
- **Templates and template parts** chosen **replace** the same template of the same theme on the other site (same slug: the Header replaces its Header, not a *Header 2* next to it), whatever **Update existing** says; one it doesn't have is added. Their navigation blocks point to the imported navigations (export them on the [Menus](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/menus/) row: the templates' navigations are suggested), their images to the imported attachments, and their links to the source site to the other site.
- **Widgets** chosen go at the **end of the same sidebar**, next to the other site's own widgets (to *Inactive widgets* when its theme has no such sidebar), each with a free number. Importing the same file again with *Update existing* updates them in place instead of adding them twice. A Navigation Menu widget points to the imported menu (export it on the [Menus](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/menus/) row), an image widget to the imported image, and the images and addresses in block widgets to the imported ones.

### From WP-CLI and the ability

```bash
wp eizport export --types=page --appearance=theme_mods:custom_logo+background_color,custom_css,widgets:text-3
wp eizport export --appearance=all --css-mode=start --no-css-markers
wp eizport export --types=page --menus=all --appearance=template_parts:header,templates:page
wp eizport import delivery.wxrz --css-mode=replace
```

A row alone takes all of it; a CSS rule's key (`r:…`) comes from [`eizport/get-export-options`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/abilities/#eizportget-export-options), which lists each row's items. The [`eizport/export`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/abilities/#eizportexport) ability takes `appearance` (row → `"all"` or keys), `css_mode` and `css_markers`.

### Limits

- The look goes to the **active theme** of the other site. Exported from one theme and imported with another, theme mods only mean something if that theme uses the same settings.
- Templates and template parts belong to their theme: imported into a site with another active theme, they wait, unused, until that theme is activated.
- Fonts installed with the Font Library aren't exported: styles that use them fall back to the other site's fonts.
- The theme mods no longer come with the Options row's *Basics* group: check **Customizer theme mods**. A block theme's site logo is an option, in *Basics*.


---

## Advanced Custom Fields

> Advanced Custom Fields (ACF) on a row of its own: its post types, taxonomies and field groups in ACF's own export format, imported before the content, and the fields that store IDs pointing to the items on the other site.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/advanced-custom-fields/

With **Advanced Custom Fields (ACF)** active (6.1 or later, the free plugin), the Export screen has an **Advanced Custom Fields (ACF)** row. Its **Choose items** panel lists what ACF registers, each with a preview:

| Item | Preview |
| --- | --- |
| **Post type** (*ACF → Post Types*) | Its name (`recipe`) |
| **Taxonomy** (*ACF → Taxonomies*) | Its name (`cuisine`) |
| **Field group** (*ACF → Field Groups*) | Its fields and their types: *Photo (image), Related (relationship)…* |

They travel in **ACF's own export format** — the JSON of *ACF → Tools → Export* — inside the bundle's `options.json`, so they need a bundle (`.wxrz`, `.zip`, as plugin or a Playground `.zip`). ACF's own posts (`acf-field-group`, `acf-post-type`…) aren't offered as content rows: this row carries them.

### Suggested

Check the posts (pages, products, an ACF post type…) and the row suggests what they use: the field groups of their values, the ACF post type of their type and the ACF taxonomies of their terms. The posts that their **post object**, **relationship** and **page link** fields point to are suggested in their own rows, and the images and files of **image** and **file** fields come along as media used.

### On the other site

1. **Before the content**, ACF imports the post types, taxonomies and field groups, as *ACF → Tools → Import* does: one with the same key there is **updated**, not duplicated, so a second delivery updates the first. The post types and taxonomies are registered at once, so their posts and terms come in.
2. The content comes in, with the values in its custom fields.
3. **When the import ends**, the fields that store IDs get the IDs the items have there:

| Field type | Points to | Mapped by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Image, File | Attachments | The imported attachments (or the ones the site already had) |
| Post Object, Relationship, Page Link | Posts, pages, any type | The imported items |
| Taxonomy | Terms | The imported terms |
| User | Users | The authors, as the importer maps them |

Only IDs that came in the file and changed are touched; a page link to a URL stays as it is. Field groups' location rules on a page or a post get its new ID too. Term values (fields shown on a taxonomy) are mapped as post values.

### What it doesn't

- **ACF PRO** (repeater, flexible content, clone, gallery, options pages, blocks) isn't covered yet.
- **Values on users** don't travel: a WXR has no users, only the authors of its posts. A user field points to a user there only when that user is an author in the file.
- **Without ACF active** on the other site, its items aren't imported (the values still come, in the custom fields).
- Field groups in the theme's **local JSON** (`acf-json/`) travel with the theme.


---

## Elementor

> Elementor with its own exporter and importer: the site settings (the Kit) and templates on a row of their own, each page's design as a .json file, and on import every image, template and link pointing to the items on the other site.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/elementor/

With **Elementor** active, Eizport carries what Elementor's own *Import / Export Kit* does — in Elementor's formats, handed to Elementor's own importer on the other site.

### The Elementor row

The **Elementor** row's **Choose items** panel lists:

| Item | What it is | Preview |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Site settings** | The active Kit: global colors and fonts, layout, theme style (*Elementor → Site Settings*), without the site's name, tagline, logo and icon — as Elementor's Kit export leaves them out | The global colors |
| **Each template** (*Templates → Saved Templates*) | A section, a page, a container… in Elementor's template file format, the one *Export template* writes | Its type |

They travel in the bundle's `options.json`, so they need a bundle (`.wxrz`, `.zip`, as plugin or a Playground `.zip`). Elementor's library (`elementor_library`) isn't offered as a content row: this row carries it.

### Pages built with Elementor

Check pages, posts — any type — built with Elementor in their own rows. With *Content as .html files* on ([Settings → Export](https://eizport.github.io/docs/settings/export-settings/)), each one's design goes as **`post_content/<slug>.json`**, in Elementor's template file format, instead of its `_elementor_data` inside the WXR; the `.html` files stay for content in blocks. With it off, the design stays in the WXR, and is handled the same way on import.

The rows suggest the rest: **Elementor** shows the site settings and the templates the pages' template widgets show as *suggested*, and the images the designs use — image and gallery widgets, backgrounds — come along as media used.

### On the other site

When the import ends, the design goes through **Elementor's own import**:

1. **Templates** are created as Elementor's Kit import creates them; a template already imported from the same site is updated instead, so a second delivery doesn't add copies.
2. **Site settings** go through Elementor's own *site settings* import: a new active Kit with the global colors and fonts added to the site's. A later delivery from the same site updates that Kit, its colors and fonts replaced by their ID instead of added again.
3. **Each page's design** goes through its document's import. Images come from the attachments the bundle brought — Elementor finds them by their source URL instead of downloading them again —, template widgets point to the imported templates, and links to the source site to this one.
4. Elementor's **generated CSS** is cleared, to be built again.

Without Elementor active on the other site, the designs are written to the pages' meta, with their images and templates mapped, ready for when Elementor is activated.

### What it doesn't

- **Elementor Pro** (Theme Builder templates and conditions, popups, forms) isn't covered yet.
- **Dynamic tags** that point to a post or a term by ID keep that ID.
- A link to a page that isn't in the file points to the same address on this site.


---

## Media

> Which attachments come with the items exported, how media files go inside bundles, and the "Only attached media" setting.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/media/

### Which attachments are exported

When you export **some** items (not all content):

1. **WordPress** adds each item's attached media (`post_parent`) and featured image (`_thumbnail_id`).
2. **The plugin** also adds the media the items **use in their content without being attached**: images, galleries, covers, files, video and audio inserted from the library. It finds them by:
   - block attributes: `"id"` (image, cover, file, video, audio), `"mediaId"` (media & text), `"ids"` (gallery);
