   - `wp-image-<id>` classes and the `[gallery ids="…"]` shortcode;
   - upload URLs, sized ones included (`-300x200`), through `attachment_url_to_postid()`.
3. **Plugins** add more with [`eizport_media_used`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/hooks/#eizport_media_used) — the WooCommerce compatibility adds product galleries.

Turn step 2 off with **Settings → Export → Only attached media**, or per export with `media_used: false`.

### Media files in the bundle

**Media files** (on by default) puts the files of every exported attachment inside the bundle, under `uploads/` with the same folders as on the old site. On import they are served to the importer from the bundle, so nothing is downloaded and the old site can be offline.

Only files in this site's uploads folder go in; offloaded media (a CDN, S3) is left to the importer to download, as usual.

### Example

A page with an attached image (A), a different featured image (B) and an image from the library in its content (C):

| Setting | Exported |
| --- | --- |
| Default | the page, A, B, C |
| Only attached media | the page, A, B |


---

## File and formats

> Choose between WordPress's plain WXR, a .wxrz or .zip bundle, a Playground .zip and a plugin that imports itself; file names and what each one holds.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/file-and-formats/

The **Format** toggle, in the **Details** panel above the list, has two choices; the first one's name follows what goes in the file.

| Shown as | File | When | Holds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **WXR XML** | `.xml` | Media files off and no options | WordPress's own export, unchanged |
| **WXR ZIP** | `.zip` | Media files or options (the default) | A [bundle as a plain .zip](https://eizport.github.io/docs/formats/zip-bundle/): the WXR, media, `post_content/`, `options.json` |
| **WXRZ** | `.wxrz` | Same, with *Bundle as .zip* off | The same [bundle as a gzipped tar](https://eizport.github.io/docs/formats/wxrz-bundle/) |
| **Playground** | `.zip` | Chosen | A [Playground blueprint bundle](https://eizport.github.io/docs/formats/playground-zip/) with themes and plugins |
| **As plugin** | `.zip` | *As plugin* on (not with Playground) | A plugin holding the bundle, which imports it on the other site with one click ([as plugin](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/as-plugin/)) |

### As plugin

The **As plugin** toggle, next to *Media files* (its ⓘ explains it), wraps the bundle in a plugin `.zip`. Install it on the other site like any plugin and click **Run import** on its row on the Plugins screen: no file to upload. See [as plugin](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/as-plugin/).

### Update existing

**Update existing**, in the **Details** panel, asks the import to update the items of the chosen content types that already exist on the other site (same type and slug) instead of adding copies — its ⓘ names those types (all of them with nothing checked), and it is disabled when only rows without content are checked: menus, options, the look. It's saved in the bundle (`update_existing` in the manifest), and the importer's box comes checked; with WP-CLI and the ability, the import updates only when asked. Not with WXR XML or Playground. See [updating items that already exist](https://eizport.github.io/docs/getting-started/importing/#updating-items-that-already-exist).

### File name

Leave it empty for WordPress's usual name, `<site name>.WordPress.<date>` — the placeholder shows the exact one for today. A name you type is sanitized and the extension is added.

### Content as .html files

With **Settings → Export → Content as .html files** (on by default), each post's content goes to `post_content/<slug>.html` instead of inside the WXR — easy to read, diff and keep under version control. On import it is put back before the importer runs. A page built with [Elementor](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/elementor/) goes as `post_content/<slug>.json` instead: its design in Elementor's format, brought in by Elementor's own import.

### Copies

Every export made on the new screen or by the ability is kept as a **copy** for a while (a day by default), with an unguessable name, and listed in [Settings → Copies](https://eizport.github.io/docs/settings/copies/).


---

## As plugin

> Export a plugin that imports its own bundle: install it on the other site, check what it needs, Run import, then delete it.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/as-plugin/

**As plugin**, next to *Media files* in the Export screen's **Details** panel, makes the file a plugin `.zip` holding the bundle. Install it on the other site like any plugin, and it imports itself — no file to upload, no importer screen to go through.

*Screenshot: The plugin's screen on the other site after Run import: everything it needs checked, the result, and "Deactivate and delete this plugin".*

### What's inside

```
mysite-wordpress-2026-10-12.zip
└── mysite-wordpress-2026-10-12-k3x9q2m7a1b8c4d6/
    ├── mysite-wordpress-2026-10-12-k3x9q2m7a1b8c4d6.php   the plugin: "Import: mysite-wordpress-2026-10-12"
    ├── readme.txt                                         what it is, as WordPress.org's Plugin Check asks
    └── mysite-wordpress-2026-10-12-k3x9q2m7a1b8c4d6.zip   the bundle (content, media, settings, as chosen)
```

The plugin's folder and file are named after the export's file name, plus the random part of the copy's name in lowercase (the same one [Copies](https://eizport.github.io/docs/settings/copies/) shows). So no file name can turn it into another plugin: an export named `woocommerce` is still `woocommerce-<random>/`, never WooCommerce's folder. Each delivery installs as its own plugin.

**Settings → Export → As plugin holds the bundle as** can put the bundle's files in the plugin instead of the bundle file — the same entries, the WXR formatted line by line, to look at or change before installing. **Next to the plugin's**, the plugin's folder is the bundle:

```
mysite-wordpress-2026-10-12.zip
└── mysite-wordpress-2026-10-12-k3x9q2m7a1b8c4d6/
    ├── mysite-wordpress-2026-10-12-k3x9q2m7a1b8c4d6.php
    ├── manifest.json
    ├── mysite.WordPress.2026-10-12.xml
    ├── post_content/home.html
    ├── options.json
    └── uploads/2026/10/photo.jpg
```

**In a bundle/ folder**, the same files go under `bundle/`, apart from the plugin's. The plugin's header (`Eizport Bundle:`) names `manifest.json` or `bundle/manifest.json`.

The default stays one file — a `.zip`, or a `.wxrz` with *Bundle as .zip* off: a smaller download, and the files can't be told apart from the plugin's. Either way, the files are reachable by URL while the plugin is installed — delete it after the import. It doesn't work with the Playground format: the toggle is off and disabled there.

### On the other site

1. **Plugins → Add Plugin → Upload Plugin**, choose the `.zip`, **Install Now**, **Activate**.
2. **Run import** on the plugin's row on the Plugins screen — or its entry in **Tools → Import**, set apart from the other importers, and a notice until it's imported — opens its screen. It isn't in the menu (a one-off import has no place there); on it, *Tools → Import* shows as the current item. While it waits, Tools → Import shows the importers' list instead of going straight to the WordPress Importer. Nothing redirects you on activation.
3. The screen lists what it needs, each with a ✓ or a link:
   - **Eizport**, active — it draws the screen and runs the import. Without it, or with a version older than the bundle needs, the same screen shows ✗ and **Install Now**, **Activate** or **Update now**, done right there; then the page reloads with what Eizport reads. Until then **What it holds** is dimmed and closed, and *Update existing* and **Run import** are disabled;
   - **the WordPress Importer**, installed — with an *Install Now* button that installs and activates it right there, like Tools → Import installs an importer (*Installing…*, *Activating…*, then ✓ and **Run import** ready);
   - **the bundle**, with its size and date;
   - **Update the items that already exist (same type and slug) instead of adding copies: Pages and Posts** — it names the content types the bundle holds, and isn't shown when it holds none — checked when the export had *Update existing* on (the plugin's `Eizport Update:` header). See [updating items that already exist](https://eizport.github.io/docs/getting-started/importing/#updating-items-that-already-exist).
4. **Run import** imports the bundle the plugin holds. The page waits while it runs (the WordPress Importer doesn't report progress), then shows how many items were imported, the settings set and the importer's messages.
5. Once imported, the screen's main button is **Deactivate and delete**: it did its job and holds a large file. Under **Also delete**, Eizport and the WordPress Importer can go in the same action — checked when they were installed for this import (the plugin notes, when activated, which were already there), unchecked otherwise. Where WordPress asks for FTP credentials to delete files, it is deactivated and you delete it from the Plugins screen.

After the import the screen doesn't offer to import again, unless the export had **Settings → Export → As plugin: allow importing again** on: then **Import again** stays, folded. Importing again finds the items already imported and doesn't duplicate them; with *Update existing*, a new delivery of the same content updates them.

The plugin is named after the export's file: *Import: EIZP-000* for `EIZP-000.zip`.

The same `.zip` also imports without installing it: upload it in **Tools → Import → WordPress**, like a `.wxrz`, or give it to `wp eizport import`. Eizport takes the bundle out of the plugin.


### Safety

The plugin imports only the bundle its own header names (`Eizport Bundle:`), from its own folder. **Run import** needs the `import` capability and a nonce; deleting needs `delete_plugins`. The plugin's code is a small file anyone can read; it downloads nothing.

In [Copies](https://eizport.github.io/docs/settings/copies/) it shows as *Plugin .zip*: it can be downloaded, not imported into the same site — install it as a plugin instead.


---

## Saved defaults

> Save the Export screen's choices as default, per user or for the whole site, on both screens.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/saved-defaults/

**Save as default** keeps everything you chose: content types with their items (or filters, on the classic screen), options, format, file name, media files and Playground themes and plugins. The Export screen opens with them, and **Reset to defaults** goes back to them. Nothing else is kept: choices you don't save are forgotten when you leave or reload the screen.

### Whose defaults

**Settings → General → Defaults are saved for**:

- **Each user** (default) — stored in user meta; anyone who can export saves their own.
- **The whole site** — one set for everyone; saving or clearing it needs `manage_options`.

### Both screens

- **New screen:** *Save as default* in the header; *Reset to defaults* goes back to them, and *Clear defaults* (active once the choices are the defaults) forgets them.
- **Classic screen:** check *Save these choices as my default* before downloading. The classic screen starts filled with the defaults too.

### Clearing

*Clear defaults* in the Export screen's header, *Clear saved defaults* in Settings → General, or the [`eizport/clear-export-defaults`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/abilities/#defaults) ability.

### What is checked

Defaults are sanitized when saved and again when loaded: unknown types and items, options that are never exported and themes or plugins no longer installed are dropped. Filters keep only the values that are set.


---

## Classic screen

> WordPress's own Tools → Export with the plugin's choices added, for those who prefer it; also on phones.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/classic-screen/

**Settings → General → Use the classic Export screen** makes Tools → Export open WordPress's own screen, with the plugin's choices added. It is always at `wp-admin/export.php?classic=1`.

It exists only while **Replace Tools → Export** is on (the default). Off, WordPress's Export screen gets nothing from the plugin, and the setting is hidden: the plugin's screen is at **Tools → Eizport**.

### What it adds

- **Several content types:** core's single choice becomes checkboxes ("All content" stays).
- **By filters or by selection** per type: WordPress's filters for posts, pages and media; the same kind for products and custom post types (dates, status, author, each taxonomy); or a checklist (a tree for pages) with a box to filter it.
- **Bundle (.wxrz or .zip):** file name, media files, settings (groups, homepage and posts page, other options by name), a Playground blueprint with themes and plugins, and a temporary copy to open by link on playground.wordpress.net.
- **Save these choices as my default**, and a screen that starts with them.

### On phones

Every checkbox and radio is a row at least 40px high to tap, the box drawn as WordPress draws it; nothing scrolls sideways.

*Screenshot: The classic screen on a phone: bundle options with 40px rows.*

### Without JavaScript

The type checkboxes stay core's radios and one type is exported, still by filters or by selection.


---

## WXRZ bundle

> The .wxrz format, entry by entry — manifest, WXR, media, post_content and options.json — and the safety rules when one is opened.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/formats/wxrz-bundle/

A `.wxrz` file is a **gzipped tar archive** (`ustar`). Any tool that reads `.tar.gz` opens it:

```bash
tar tzvf site.wxrz        # list
tar xzf site.wxrz -C out  # extract
```

### Entries

```text
manifest.json                      required, first
<site>.WordPress.<date>.xml        the WXR (WordPress eXtended RSS)
options.json                       optional: settings
post_content/<slug>.html           optional: one per post with content
post_content/<slug>.json           optional: one per page built with Elementor, its design
uploads/2026/10/photo.jpg          optional: media files, as in wp-content/uploads
```

### manifest.json

Its [JSON Schema](https://eizport.github.io/schemas/1.1/manifest.json) is named in the manifest's `$schema`, so a code editor (VS Code, PhpStorm…) checks a manifest edited by hand and completes its keys; Eizport checks it against the same schema before importing, and says which key is wrong. Each version has its own, frozen once released; [`schemas/trunk/manifest.json`](https://eizport.github.io/schemas/trunk/manifest.json) is always the newest.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://eizport.github.io/schemas/1.1/manifest.json",
  "format": "wxrz",
  "version": 2,
  "requires": "1.1.0",
  "generator": "Eizport 1.1.0",
  "site": "https://example.com/",
  "created": "2026-10-10T22:11:50+00:00",
  "wxr": [ "example.WordPress.2026-10-10.xml" ],
  "files": {
    "https://example.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/photo.jpg": "uploads/2026/10/photo.jpg"
  },
  "options": "options.json",
  "update_existing": true,
  "term_media": {
    "product_cat": { "western": { "thumbnail_id": 13 } }
  },
  "post_content": {
    "home.html": { "id": 43, "type": "page", "slug": "home" }
  }
}
```

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `$schema` | The schema's URL, for editors |
| `format`, `version` | Always `"wxrz"`; the layout's version — `2` since Eizport 1.1.0, `1` before. A reader takes the versions it knows and refuses newer ones |
| `requires` | The oldest Eizport that reads it (`1.1.0`); rises only when the layout does. An older Eizport refuses the bundle and says to update — Eizport 1.0.x refuses it as having no valid manifest |
| `generator`, `site`, `created` | Who made it (`Eizport <version>`, shown on a bundle plugin's screen), from where, when |
| `wxr` | The WXR entry's name (the first one is read) |
| `files` | Attachment URL in the WXR → entry in the archive. The importer's download of that URL is answered with the entry |
| `options` | The options file's entry, when there is one |
| `update_existing` | `true` when the import should update the items that already exist (same type and slug): the importer's box comes checked. WP-CLI and the ability update only when asked |
| `term_media` | Taxonomy → term slug → meta key → attachment ID on the exporting site, for the terms the items use ([`eizport_term_media`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/hooks/#eizport_term_media)); mapped to the imported attachment at the end of the import |
| `post_content` | Content file → the item it belongs to: original `id`, `type` and `slug` |

### options.json

```json
{
  "format": "eizport-options",
  "version": 1,
  "options": {
    "show_on_front": "page",
    "page_on_front": "43",
    "blogname": "Example"
  },
  "post_ids": [ "page_on_front" ]
}
```

`options` are set with `update_option()` when the import ends. Each name in `post_ids` holds a post ID: it gets the ID the importer gave that post, or is left out if the post wasn't imported.

### post_content/

Each file is the item's `post_content`, byte for byte; in the WXR, the item's `<content:encoded>` is empty. On import, the content is put back into the WXR item with the same original ID (else the same type and slug) before the importer reads it. The [`eizport_post_content`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/hooks/#eizport_post_content) filter can change it.

### Opening a bundle safely

When a bundle is imported:

- only entries the manifest lists, plus `post_content/` files and `options.json`, are written;
- every media entry must be under `uploads/`, with no `..`, backslash, null byte or `//`, and a file type WordPress allows to be uploaded (`wp_check_filetype()`): never PHP;
- everything goes to a new private folder in `wp-content/uploads/eizport/tmp/`, deleted after the import;
- the archive may expand to **512 MB** at most (filter [`eizport_wxrz_max_bytes`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/hooks/#eizport_wxrz_max_bytes)), read in steps, against decompression bombs;
- entry names longer than `ustar` allows are skipped on export: the importer downloads those files instead.

> Only import files you trust, as with any WXR: a bundle can't run code, but its content and settings become your site's.


---

## ZIP bundle

> The same bundle as a plain .zip, which any computer opens — how to turn it on and how it is read.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/formats/zip-bundle/

By default (**Settings → Export → Bundle as .zip**, on), bundles are plain `.zip` files instead of `.wxrz` — inside a plugin made as plugin too. The entries are **exactly the same** — `manifest.json`, the WXR, `options.json`, `post_content/`, `uploads/` — so everything on the [WXRZ page](https://eizport.github.io/docs/formats/wxrz-bundle/) applies.

### Why

A `.zip` opens with a double click on any computer; `.wxrz` needs a tool that reads `.tar.gz`. Choose `.zip` when people will look inside the file; keep `.wxrz` when it only travels between sites.

### Per export

The setting is the default. The [`eizport/export`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/abilities/#eizportexport) ability takes `zip: true` or `zip: false` for one export.

### How it is written and read

The plugin writes the tar bundle and turns it into a `.zip` (with `ZipArchive`, or core's PclZip), and on import turns a `.zip` back into a tar before reading it — one code path for both, with the same checks:

- only bundle entries are taken (the manifest, a top-level `.xml`, `options.json`, `post_content/*.html`, safe `uploads/` files);
- the uncompressed size counts against the same 512 MB limit.

### Telling bundles from Playground files

Both end in `.zip`. A bundle has `manifest.json` and no `blueprint.json`; a Playground `.zip` has `blueprint.json`. The importer and the Copies list tell them apart that way.


---

## Playground zip

> A WordPress Playground blueprint bundle that boots a site with the exported content, media, theme and plugins — how it's built and how to run it.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/formats/playground-zip/

With the **Playground** format, the export is a `.zip` ready for [WordPress Playground](https://wordpress.org/playground/): a blueprint bundle that installs the themes and plugins you chose and imports the content.

*Screenshot: Playground themes and plugins: what the .zip installs.*

### Run it

```bash
npx @wp-playground/cli@latest server --blueprint=./site.zip
```

Or open its link on playground.wordpress.net (new screen: the **Open in Playground** action in [Copies](https://eizport.github.io/docs/settings/copies/); classic screen: *Keep a copy to open by link*). The copy is served with the CORS headers Playground needs.

**Even from a local server.** Playground runs in your browser, so a copy made on WordPress Studio or any `localhost` site opens on playground.wordpress.net without uploading it anywhere — the browser fetches it from your machine (the link works on your computer only).

### Playground options

**Details → Playground options** (enabled with the Playground format) opens three groups, one at a time; the button counts what's set.

### Landing page

Where Playground opens once the site is ready — **Home page** (the default), **Dashboard**, **A page** of this site, or **A path** (`/shop/`). A page goes in the blueprint as a relative path, `/?pagename=<its path>`, so it opens the same page whatever ID it gets in Playground. (Without it, Playground itself would open the dashboard.)

### Language

The language Playground opens in — **Site language** (the default), **Your language** (shown when your profile's is another one) or **English (United States)**. In another language than English, the blueprint runs Playground's `setSiteLanguage` step after the installs: it sets the site's language and fetches the translations of WordPress and of the themes and plugins from the WordPress.org directory. The translations this site has of the others — premium, custom — go inside the `.zip`. A language this site hasn't installed isn't offered.

### Themes and plugins

Any **installed** theme or plugin can go in. Plugins are installed **active or inactive as they are on this site**; of the themes, this site's is activated (when chosen), and a child theme brings its parent. The ones from the WordPress.org directory aren't copied: the blueprint installs them from the directory, **in the version this site has** (`woocommerce.11.2.1.zip`), when the directory has that version — a release, not newer than the directory's. The others — premium, custom, in-house, and a development, beta or RC version (`1.1.0-dev`) — are zipped from the site into the bundle, and Playground installs them from there. WordPress's own update check says which ones are from the directory.

**Must-use plugins** (`wp-content/mu-plugins/`) are listed too, when the site has any: each one chosen goes inside the `.zip`, with the folder it loads (`require __DIR__ . '/<folder>/…'`, or a `<name>/` folder next to `<name>.php`). The ones the platform puts there — WordPress Studio's SQLite loader, hosts' loaders — and Eizport's own temporary ones aren't offered; the [`eizport_playground_mu_plugins`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/hooks/#eizport_playground_mu_plugins) filter changes the list.

> **Use it responsibly.** Premium and custom themes and plugins are copied into the file. Share a Playground `.zip` only where their licenses allow — keep the ones with paid licenses to yourself or your team.

### Inside

```text
blueprint.json
<site>.WordPress.<date>.xml        the plain WXR (content inside, not in post_content/)
uploads/…                          media files, when Media files is on
post_content/…                     content files, when Content as .html files is on
themes/<stylesheet>.zip            each theme chosen that isn't in the directory (a child brings its parent)
plugins/<slug>.zip                 each plugin chosen that isn't in the directory
languages/plugins|themes/…         their translations, in a language other than English
mu-plugins/<file>.php              each must-use plugin chosen
mu-plugins/<folder>.zip            each folder they load
```

### What the blueprint does

1. Installs the themes (parents first) — from the directory or from the bundle — and activates the active one, if chosen, else the first.
2. Installs and activates the plugins, the same way.
3. In another language: sets it (`setSiteLanguage`, which fetches the directory's translations) and writes the bundled ones.
4. Writes the must-use plugins and unzips their folders into `wp-content/mu-plugins/`, before the import: the post types and taxonomies they register are there for it.
5. Writes the media and content files and two temporary must-use plugins: one answers the importer's media downloads from the files and puts each `.html` back into its post (`wp_import_post_data_raw`); the other sets the options when the import ends, with IDs mapped.
6. Runs `importWxr` (Playground installs the WordPress Importer itself).
7. Removes the temporary plugins and files.

The [`eizport_playground_blueprint`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/hooks/#eizport_playground_blueprint) filter changes the blueprint before it is written.


---

## General

> The plugin's Settings → General — whether Tools → Export is replaced, the classic screen, saved defaults and how long copies are kept.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/settings/general/

*Screenshot: The plugin's Settings → General.*

The plugin's settings open from the **Settings** link in its row in **Plugins** (`wp-admin/plugins.php?page=eizport-settings-wp-admin`); they have no item in the Settings menu.

### Export screen

| Setting | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Replace Tools → Export** | On | Tools → Export opens the plugin's Export screen. Off, WordPress's Export screen stays as it is, with nothing added, and the plugin's is at **Tools → Eizport** |
| **Use the classic Export screen** | Off | Only while Tools → Export is replaced. | Tools → Export opens WordPress's own screen with the plugin's choices, instead of the new one ([classic screen](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/classic-screen/)) |
| **Defaults are saved for** | Each user | Or *The whole site* ([saved defaults](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/saved-defaults/)) |

### Import screen

| Setting | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Open the WordPress Importer from Tools → Import** | On | Tools → Import goes straight to the WordPress Importer, when it is active; its screen links to **All importers** (`import.php?all=1`). Off, Tools → Import lists them, as WordPress does |
| **Style Tools → Import → WordPress** | On | The WordPress Importer looks like the plugin's Export screen: a header with the main button, its steps in cards, and a file button in the admin's language. Off, it looks as WordPress made it; `.wxrz` bundles are accepted either way ([importing](https://eizport.github.io/docs/getting-started/importing/)) |

*Clear saved defaults* forgets them (the current user's, or the site's).

### Copies

**Keep copies for**: 1 hour, 12 hours, **1 day** (default), 1 week, or until deleted. After that a copy stops being served and is deleted by a cron event (and on the next use, where cron doesn't run). Copies already kept follow a new choice too. Developers can override it with [`eizport_copy_lifetime`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/hooks/#eizport_copy_lifetime).

### Who can change them

Settings need `manage_options`. The page itself opens for anyone who can export (to see the copies).


---

## Export settings

> The plugin's Settings → Export — attached media, linked settings, .zip bundles and content as .html files.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/settings/export-settings/

*Screenshot: The plugin's Settings → Export.*

All in one card, **With the items exported**:

| Setting | Default | Per export (`eizport/export`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Only attached media** — items bring only their attached media and featured images, as WordPress does, not the media used in their content ([media](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/media/)) | Off | `media_used` |
| **Linked settings** — when settings that point to the items exported come along: when items are checked and on export, when checked, on export, never ([options](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/options/#linked-settings)) | Both | `options.linked` |
| **Bundle as .zip** — bundles are plain `.zip` instead of `.wxrz` ([ZIP bundle](https://eizport.github.io/docs/formats/zip-bundle/)), inside a plugin made [as plugin](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/as-plugin/) too | On | `zip` |
| **As plugin: allow importing again** — a plugin exported [as plugin](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/as-plugin/) still offers *Import again* once it imported | Off | — |
| **As plugin holds the bundle as** — in a plugin exported [as plugin](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/as-plugin/): one file (`.zip`, or `.wxrz` with *Bundle as .zip* off), or its files next to the plugin's, or in a `bundle/` folder | One file | — |
| **Content as .html files** — each post's content in `post_content/<slug>.html` (a page built with Elementor: its design in `<slug>.json`) | On | `post_content` |
| **Mark imported CSS** — CSS rules from the [look's rows](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/appearance/) go between `/* head … */` and `/* tail … */` comments named after the file, to show where they came from; the importer can change it | On | `css_markers` |


---

## Copies

> The exports kept on the site — download, open in Playground, copy the link, import, delete — and how their links work.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/settings/copies/

*Screenshot: The plugin's Settings → Copies: a .wxrz, a .zip bundle and a Playground .zip.*

Every export from the new screen or the ability is kept as a copy in `wp-content/uploads/eizport/tmp/`, listed like the Media Library: search, sort, filter by format.

### Actions

| Action | For |
| --- | --- |
| **Open in Playground** | Playground `.zip` copies: opens playground.wordpress.net with the copy's link |
| **Download** | Every copy |
| **Copy link** | Every copy: anyone with the link can download it until it expires |
| **Import** | Bundles and WXR files: imports into this site |
| **Delete permanently** | One, several (check them) or **Delete all** in the header |

### Links and privacy

A copy's link is meant to be shared with Playground or a teammate, not found by anyone else:

- **A token like a password:** the name ends in a random 16-character token (`site-w9bjZ9pyEWxC8VMf.zip`, from a cryptographic generator), so the link can't be guessed. The list shows the name without it (`site.zip`); hovering shows it whole.
- **Served by PHP, only until it expires:** the link goes through WordPress (`?eizport_playground=<name>`), which checks the expiry and sends the CORS headers Playground needs.
- **Out of search engines:** the response carries `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow, noarchive`, and the site's `robots.txt` gets `Disallow` rules for the copies' folder and links.
- **No direct access:** `uploads/eizport/.htaccess` denies direct requests on Apache and LiteSpeed, and every folder has an `index.php`, so nothing is listed. On nginx, `.htaccess` doesn't apply; deny `/wp-content/uploads/eizport/` in the server's configuration for the same effect — the token, the expiry and robots.txt still protect the files.

Don't keep copies of content that must stay private.

### On a local site

Copies made on a local site (WordPress Studio, `localhost`) open on playground.wordpress.net too: Playground runs **in your browser**, which can reach your local server. The link works only on your computer — perfect for testing a demo before sharing it.

### Cleanup

Expired copies are deleted by a cron event and on the next use; the `tmp/` folder itself goes once it is empty. Uninstalling the plugin deletes `uploads/eizport/`.


---

## AI agents

> Let an AI agent export, import and manage copies for you: the abilities over MCP, what to ask, what the agent sees, and the safety built in.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/ai-agents/

Eizport is **agent-first**: everything the screens do is an [ability](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/abilities/) of the WordPress Abilities API — a named action with a JSON Schema for its input and output, a permission check, and hints saying whether it only reads or deletes. That is exactly what an AI agent needs to act on a site safely, without screen scraping.

### Connect an agent

1. Install the [MCP Adapter](https://github.com/WordPress/mcp-adapter) on the site. It exposes abilities as **MCP tools**.
2. Connect your MCP client (an AI assistant, an IDE agent, a CLI agent) to the site as described in the adapter's docs, with a user who can export (and import, if the agent should import).
3. Ask in plain words. The agent lists the `eizport/*` tools, reads their schemas, and calls them.

On a local [WordPress Studio](https://developer.wordpress.com/studio/) site, Studio's own MCP server can run the same abilities through its `wp_cli` tool (`wp eval`, see [WP-CLI](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/wp-cli/)).

### What to ask

| You ask | The agent calls |
| --- | --- |
| “What can I export from this site?” | `eizport/get-export-options` |
| “Which page is the homepage, and which ones are the shop and checkout?” | `eizport/get-items` (`roles` on each item) |
| “Export the homepage with its images and the basic settings as a .zip.” | `eizport/get-items`, then `eizport/export` with `types`, `options.groups: ["basics"]`, `zip: true` |
| “Export every published product in the Shoes category, for Playground, with WooCommerce.” | `eizport/get-export-options` (term ID), then `eizport/export` with `filters` and `blueprint.plugins` |
| “Which settings mention the newsletter?” | `eizport/get-options` with `search` |
| “List the copies and delete the ones older than a day.” | `eizport/get-copies`, then `eizport/delete-copies` |
| “Import the store-products copy here.” | `eizport/import` with `copy` |
| “Save this as my default export.” | `eizport/save-export-defaults` |

### What the agent sees

Each tool carries its **description**, its **input schema** (types, enums, defaults, required fields) and its **output schema**, and the MCP annotations:

- **read-only** — `get-export-options`, `get-items`, `get-options`, `get-copies`, `get-export-defaults`, `get-settings`: safe to call while exploring;
- **destructive** — `delete-copies`, `clear-export-defaults`: a well-behaved agent asks before calling them;
- **idempotent** — calling again changes nothing more.

Errors come back as codes an agent can act on: `eizport_invalid_type` (a post type that can't be exported), `eizport_invalid_options` (an option that is never exported), `eizport_invalid_blueprint` (a theme or plugin not installed), `eizport_export_unavailable` (one export per request: call again).

### Safety built in

- **WordPress's permissions:** the agent can only do what its user can — `export` for exports and copies, `import` to import, `manage_options` for settings.
- **No secrets leave:** site URLs, the admin email, keys and salts, users and roles, active plugins, transients and caches are never exported, whatever the agent asks — nor options, theme mods or widget fields named like secrets (passwords, tokens, API and license keys).
- **Copies are temporary and hidden:** a random 16-character token in each link, `noindex` and robots.txt, a folder locked against direct access, and deletion when they expire ([copies](https://eizport.github.io/docs/settings/copies/)).
- **Imports merge**, they don't overwrite the site.

### Docs for agents

This documentation is written for agents too:

- [`/llms.txt`](https://eizport.github.io/llms.txt) — an index of every page, with descriptions, linking to Markdown versions;
- [`/llms-full.txt`](https://eizport.github.io/llms-full.txt) — the whole documentation in one file;
- every page as Markdown — the same URL ending in `.md` (see “View as Markdown” at the bottom of each page).

Point your agent at `llms.txt` and it knows the plugin before its first call.


---

## Abilities

> Every eizport/* ability of the WordPress Abilities API — input, output, permission — over REST, PHP and MCP.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/abilities/

Everything the screens do is an **ability** of the [Abilities API](https://developer.wordpress.org/apis/abilities/) (WordPress 6.9+), in the category `eizport`. The Export and Settings screens call them too, so code, AI agents and the UI share one path.

### Calling them

**REST** (`/wp-json/wp-abilities/v1/abilities/<name>/run`, authenticated: cookie + nonce, or an application password):

```bash
curl -u admin:APP_PASSWORD -X POST \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://example.com/wp-json/wp-abilities/v1/abilities/eizport/export/run \
  -d '{"input":{"types":{"page":{"ids":[43]}},"options":{"groups":["basics"]}}}'
```

Read-only abilities run with `GET` and the input in the query string.

**PHP**:

```php
$copy = wp_get_ability( 'eizport/export' )->execute(
	array(
		'types' => array( 'product' => array( 'filters' => array( 'status' => 'publish' ) ) ),
		'zip'   => true,
	)
);
if ( ! is_wp_error( $copy ) ) {
	echo $copy['download_url'];
}
```

**MCP**: with the [MCP adapter](https://github.com/WordPress/mcp-adapter), each ability is a tool an AI agent can call.

> One export runs per request: `export_wp()` defines its helpers inside itself. A second `eizport/export` in the same request returns `eizport_export_unavailable`.

### Overview

| Ability | Does | Permission | Annotations |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eizport/get-export-options` | What can be exported | `export` | readonly |
| `eizport/get-items` | A page of one type's items | `export` | readonly |
| `eizport/get-options` | The site's options, one by one | `export` | readonly |
| `eizport/get-suggestions` | What the items chosen suggest | `export` | readonly |
| `eizport/get-reviews` | A page of product reviews | `export` | readonly |
| `eizport/export` | Exports to a copy | `export` | — |
| `eizport/get-copies` | The copies kept | `export` | readonly |
| `eizport/delete-copies` | Deletes copies | `export` | destructive, idempotent |
| `eizport/import` | Imports a copy or a media file | `import` | — |
| `eizport/get-export-defaults` | The saved defaults | `export` | readonly |
| `eizport/save-export-defaults` | Saves defaults | `export` (site's: `manage_options`) | idempotent |
| `eizport/clear-export-defaults` | Forgets them | as above | destructive |
| `eizport/get-settings` | The plugin's settings | `manage_options` | readonly |
| `eizport/update-settings` | Changes settings | `manage_options` | idempotent |

### eizport/get-export-options

No input. Returns `types` (each with `type`, `label`, `count`, `hierarchical`, `statuses` and `taxonomies` with their terms), `option_groups` (`group`, `label`, `options`), `front_pages` (`front`, `posts` IDs), `themes`, `plugins`, `copy_lifetime` (seconds), `filename` (today's default name), `linked` (the linked settings mode), `bundle_zip`, `review_count` (approved product reviews; 0 without WooCommerce) `appearance` (`theme_mods`, `custom_css`, `global_styles`, `global_css`, `templates`, `template_parts`, `widgets`, `advanced-custom-fields`, `elementor` → their items: `key`, `label`, `details`, `preview`; see [Appearance](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/appearance/)) and `menus`: `classic` (`id`, `name`, `slug`, `items`, `locations` — the labels of the theme locations it sits in) and `navigation` (`id`, `title`, `links`) — see [Menus](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/menus/).

### eizport/get-items

| Input | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | string, required | A post type from `get-export-options` |
| `search` | string | |
| `page`, `per_page` | integer | `per_page` up to 100 |
| `orderby` | `date` \| `title` \| `menu_order` | |
| `order` | `asc` \| `desc` | |
| `filters` | object | `author`, `start_date`/`end_date` (`YYYY-MM`), `status`, `terms` (term IDs) |
| `include` | integer[] | Only these items (none: an empty page) |

Returns `items` — `id`, `title`, `status`, `date`, `parent`, `author`, `file` (attachments), `roles` (`option`, `label`, `with`) — plus `total` and `total_pages`.

### eizport/get-options

Input: `search`, `group` (a key of `option_groups`), `names` (only these), `page`, `per_page`. Returns `items` (`name`, `size`, `value` — in a line, arrays as JSON, up to 200 characters — `autoload`, `post_id`), `total`, `total_pages`. Options that are never exported and transients are left out.

### eizport/get-suggestions

Input: `types` (as `eizport/export` takes them), `whole` (post types chosen whole, the same as `{}` in `types`) and `menus.classic` (menus chosen). Returns `items` (post type → IDs the items' content uses, through [`eizport_suggested_items`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/hooks/#eizport_suggested_items), and the pages and posts the menus chosen link to), `reviews` (approved reviews of the products chosen), `options` (settings pointing to the items, unless *Linked settings* is *Never* or *On export*), `appearance` (row → the keys of its items, all suggested) and `menus` (`classic`: the menus in theme locations; `navigation`: the navigations the items' content or the theme's templates use). Nothing is added to an export by itself.

### eizport/get-reviews

Input: `search`, `include` (only these), `page`, `per_page`. Returns `items` (`id`, `author`, `product`, `product_title`, `rating`, `excerpt`, `date`), `total`, `total_pages`; empty without WooCommerce.

### eizport/export

| Input | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `types` | object: post type → `{ "ids": [...] }` or `{ "filters": {...} }` | all content |
| `media` | boolean: media files inside | `true` |
| `media_used` | boolean: media used in content | `true` unless *Only attached media* |
| `post_content` | boolean: `post_content/*.html` | *Content as .html files* |
| `bundle` | boolean: `false` for WordPress's plain `.xml` | `true` |
| `zip` | boolean: `.zip` instead of `.wxrz` | *Bundle as .zip* |
| `options` | object: `groups`, `names`, `all`, `front_pages`, `linked` | none |
| `blueprint` | object: `themes`, `plugins` (installed active or inactive as on this site), `mu_plugins` (must-use plugin files, as `get-export-options` lists them), `landing_page` (`"home"`, `"admin"`, `{ "page": ID }` or a path like `"/shop/"`), `language` (`"site"`, the default, `"user"`, `"en_US"` or an installed locale like `"pt_BR"`) — makes a Playground `.zip` | — |
| `as_plugin` | boolean: a plugin `.zip` that imports its bundle ([as plugin](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/as-plugin/)); not with `blueprint` | `false` |
| `update_existing` | boolean: ask the import to update the items that already exist (same type and slug); saved in the bundle | `false` |
| `reviews` | object: `ids` (comment IDs; `[]` for none) or `all` — WooCommerce product reviews | all of the products' reviews |
| `appearance` | object: row (`theme_mods`, `custom_css`, `global_styles`, `global_css`, `templates`, `template_parts`, `widgets`, and [`advanced-custom-fields`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/advanced-custom-fields/) with ACF active, [`elementor`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/elementor/) with Elementor active) → `"all"` or the keys of its items (from `eizport/get-export-options`); a list of rows means each whole — the site's [look](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/appearance/), with the media it uses; needs `bundle` | none |
| `css_mode` | `end`, `start`, `replace` (the head/tail blocks of the same name the other site has; at the end with none) or `replace_all`: how the CSS rules are added on import; whoever imports can change it | `end` |
| `css_markers` | head/tail comments around the CSS rules | Settings → Export |
| `menus` | object: `classic` (menu term IDs, with their items and theme locations), `navigation` (`wp_navigation` IDs), or `all` — [menus](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/menus/) | none (*all content* has them) |
| `filename` | string, without extension | `<site>.WordPress.<date>` |

Returns the copy:

```json
{
  "name": "site-w9bjZ9pyEWxC8VMf.zip",
  "format": "playground",
  "size": 8178533,
  "created": "2026-10-10T22:11:58+00:00",
  "expires": "2026-10-11T22:11:58+00:00",
  "download_url": "https://example.com/?eizport_playground=site-w9bjZ9pyEWxC8VMf.zip",
  "playground_url": "https://playground.wordpress.net/?blueprint-url=…",
  "command": "npx @wp-playground/cli@latest server --blueprint=./site-w9bjZ9pyEWxC8VMf.zip"
}
```

`format` is `wxrz`, `zip`, `wxr`, `playground` or `plugin`; `expires` is `""` for copies kept until deleted. Errors: `eizport_invalid_type`, `eizport_invalid_options` (an option that is never exported), `eizport_invalid_blueprint` (a theme or plugin not installed), `eizport_export_unavailable`.

### eizport/get-copies and eizport/delete-copies

`get-copies` returns the list of copies, as above. `delete-copies` takes `names` (as `get-copies` returns them) or `all: true`, and returns `{ "deleted": 3 }`.

### eizport/import

Input: `copy` (a copy's name) or `attachment_id` (a `.wxrz`, `.zip`, `.xml` or `.xml.gz` in the media library). `update_existing` (boolean) updates the items that already exist (same type and slug) instead of adding copies; default: no — the bundle never decides it on its own. `options` (names) sets the bundle's options outside the [option groups](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/options/#options-outside-the-groups-on-import) too; default: none. `css_mode` (`end`, `start`, `replace` — the head/tail blocks of the same name this site has, or at the end when there are none —, `replace_all`) and `css_markers` (boolean) change how the bundle's CSS rules are added ([appearance](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/appearance/)); default: what the bundle asks. Needs the WordPress Importer installed. A plugin made [as plugin](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/as-plugin/) is refused (`eizport_plugin_zip`): install it as a plugin. Returns `posts` (how many the importer created or found), `options` (the names set) and `log` (the importer's messages, as text).

### Defaults

- `eizport/get-export-defaults` — no input; returns `{ "types": …, "settings": … }` or `{}`.
- `eizport/save-export-defaults` — input `types` and `settings` (the Export screen's state: `format`, `filename`, `media`, `option_names`, `option_groups`, `option_all`, `include_suggested`, `review_ids`, `review_all`, `as_plugin`, `update_existing`, `themes`, `plugins`); returns what was saved, sanitized.
- `eizport/clear-export-defaults` — no input.

### Settings

`eizport/get-settings` returns `copy_lifetime`, `replace_export`, `classic_ui`, `style_import`, `content_files`, `attached_only`, `bundle_zip`, `defaults_scope`, `linked_options`, and the choices of each (`lifetime_choices`, `scope_choices`, `linked_choices`). `eizport/update-settings` takes any of those (values from the choices) and returns them all; unknown keys are refused.


---

## Hooks

> Every filter and action of Eizport, with its parameters and an example.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/hooks/

All hooks are prefixed `eizport_`. Add them from a plugin or a theme's `functions.php`.

### eizport_linked_options

Options that point to a post, with the role they give it. They get the imported post's ID on import, show as a badge on the item, and can come with it ([linked settings](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/options/#linked-settings)).

```php
add_filter( 'eizport_linked_options', function ( array $linked ) {
	$linked['my_plugin_landing_page'] = array(
		'label' => __( 'Landing page', 'my-plugin' ),     // The role, shown as a badge.
		'with'  => array( 'my_plugin_landing_enabled' ),  // Options that go with it.
		'when'  => array( 'my_plugin_mode' => 'landing' ), // Only while these hold these values.
	);
	return $linked;
} );
```

| Param | |
| --- | --- |
| `array $linked` | Option name → `label` (string), `with` (string[], optional), `when` (option → value, optional) |

### eizport_option_groups

The groups of options offered on the screens and in `options.groups`.

```php
add_filter( 'eizport_option_groups', function ( array $groups ) {
	$groups['my-plugin'] = array(
		'label'   => __( 'My Plugin: layout and colors', 'my-plugin' ), // "Name: what it holds".
		'options' => array( 'my_plugin_layout', 'my_plugin_colors' ),
	);
	return $groups;
} );
```

### eizport_denied_options

More options never exported — keys, tokens, licenses, version numbers. Returns names to **add**; WordPress's own denied options can't be removed.

```php
add_filter( 'eizport_denied_options', function ( array $names ) {
	return array_merge( $names, array( 'my_plugin_api_key', 'my_plugin_db_version' ) );
} );
```

### eizport_is_secret

Whether a name — an option, a theme mod, a widget field — holds a secret, so it's never exported nor listed. By default: names with `secret`, `password`, `token`, `api_key`, `license`, `private`, `credential`, `access_key`, `auth_key` or `webhook`, and plugins' known stores of them (WP Mail SMTP, payment gateways). Mark your own, or let one through:

```php
add_filter( 'eizport_is_secret', function ( bool $secret, string $name ) {
	return 'my_plugin_connection' === $name ? true : $secret;
}, 10, 2 );
```

### eizport_media_used

Attachments a post uses beyond what its content names, like a gallery stored in meta. Runs when some items are exported and *Only attached media* is off.

```php
add_filter( 'eizport_media_used', function ( array $used, WP_Post $post ) {
	if ( 'portfolio' === $post->post_type ) {
		$used = array_merge( $used, wp_parse_id_list( get_post_meta( $post->ID, 'gallery', true ) ) );
	}
	return $used;
}, 10, 2 );
```

### eizport_term_media

Term meta that hold an attachment ID, by taxonomy, like a category's image. The attachments go with the export (for the terms the items use), the manifest lists them (`term_media`), and the import points them to the imported attachments. The WooCommerce compatibility adds `product_cat` → `thumbnail_id`.

```php
add_filter( 'eizport_term_media', function ( array $keys ) {
	$keys['portfolio_type'][] = 'cover_id';
	return $keys;
} );
```

Pair it with [`eizport_media_used`](#eizport_media_used), which adds the attachments to the export.

### eizport_updated_from_import

Fires after an existing post was updated from an imported item, with *Update existing* on. Use it to update what a plugin keeps elsewhere.

```php
add_action( 'eizport_updated_from_import', function ( int $id, array $post ) {
	clean_post_cache( $id );
}, 10, 2 );
```

### eizport_block_id_attributes

Blocks whose attributes hold post IDs, mapped to the imported items when an import ends (core's Image, Gallery, Cover, Media & Text, File, Video, Audio and navigation links are there already). Add a plugin's block by its full name.

```php
add_filter( 'eizport_block_id_attributes', function ( array $blocks ) {
	$blocks['my-plugin/card'] = array( 'imageId', 'postIds' ); // A number or an array of numbers.
	return $blocks;
} );
```

### eizport_menus_update_existing

Whether an import replaces the items of the classic menus the site already has (`true`) or leaves them as they are (`false`, the default). *Update existing* turns it on for its import.

```php
add_filter( 'eizport_menus_update_existing', '__return_true' );
```

### eizport_suggested_items

Posts an item suggests exporting too, like the products a block in its content shows. The Export screen shows them as *N suggested* in their type's row ([choosing items](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/choosing-items/#suggestions)); nothing is added by itself. The WooCommerce compatibility uses it for products.

```php
add_filter( 'eizport_suggested_items', function ( array $suggested, WP_Post $post ) {
	// A "related" block stores the post IDs it shows.
	if ( preg_match_all( '/"relatedIds":\[([\d,]+)\]/', $post->post_content, $m ) ) {
		foreach ( $m[1] as $list ) {
			$suggested = array_merge( $suggested, wp_parse_id_list( $list ) );
		}
	}
	return $suggested;
}, 10, 2 );
```

Only posts of types that can be exported are suggested.

### eizport_content_types

The post types the Export screen offers as rows: post type => value of core's *content* radio. A plugin takes out its own types that travel another way (the Advanced Custom Fields compatibility removes ACF's field groups, post types and taxonomies).

### eizport_look_items

The items of a row next to the look's (`$items`, `$row`): a plugin fills its own row, each item with `key`, `label`, `details` and `preview` (`type` and `value`). Used by the Advanced Custom Fields compatibility for the `advanced-custom-fields` row.

### eizport_look_data

The options file's data for such a row (`$out`, `$row`, `$keys`: the item keys chosen): the row's entry goes in `$out`.

### eizport_look_suggested

The keys such a row suggests for the posts chosen (`$keys`, `$row`, `$chosen`: post type => IDs).

### eizport_look_media

The attachments the look chosen uses (`$ids`, `$choice`): a plugin's row adds the ones its items use (the Elementor row: images of templates and site settings).

### eizport_content_file

The file a post's content goes to with *Content as .html files* on (`$file`, `$post`): `null` for `post_content/<slug>.html`, or `array( 'extension' => 'json', 'data' => … )` for a page builder's design in its own format — the post's content then stays in the WXR, and the importer keeps the `.json` for whoever applies it when the import ends (`$GLOBALS['eizport_content_data']`, by the item's original ID). The Elementor compatibility uses it.

### eizport_advanced_custom_fields_id_types

The ACF field types whose values are IDs an import maps: type => `post`, `term` or `user`. Add a plugin's own field type:

```php
add_filter( 'eizport_advanced_custom_fields_id_types', function ( array $types ) {
	$types['my_product_picker'] = 'post';
	return $types;
} );
```

### eizport_register_compat

Action, on `plugins_loaded` (priority 20), where compatibilities hook the filters above. See [compatibilities](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/compatibilities/).

### eizport_post_id_options

Options that hold a post ID, mapped on import. By default, the keys of `eizport_linked_options`; kept for compatibility.

| Param | |
| --- | --- |
| `string[] $names` | Option names |

### eizport_post_content

The content an imported item gets from its `post_content/` file.

| Param | |
| --- | --- |
| `string\|null $content` | The file's content, or `null` when there is none |
| `array $item` | `id` (original ID), `type`, `slug` |
| `string $dir` | Folder the bundle was unpacked into |

### eizport_wxrz_max_bytes

The most a bundle may expand to when imported. Default `512 * MB_IN_BYTES`.

### eizport_playground_blueprint

The blueprint of a Playground `.zip`, before it is written.

| Param | |
| --- | --- |
| `array $blueprint` | The blueprint (`steps`, `landingPage`…) |
| `string $wxr_name` | The WXR's name inside the `.zip` |

### eizport_playground_mu_plugins

The must-use plugins a Playground `.zip` can take — without the platform's (WordPress Studio, hosts) and Eizport's own. Take a host's loader out, or put back one left out.

| Param | |
| --- | --- |
| `array $choices` | File => plugin data, as `get_mu_plugins()` gives them |

### eizport_selection_limit

How many items each *By selection* list of the classic screen shows (the latest). Default `1000`.

### eizport_copy_lifetime

How long a copy lasts, in seconds; `0` keeps copies until deleted. Default: the one chosen in Settings.


---

## Compatibilities

> Which plugins are supported (WooCommerce, Advanced Custom Fields, Elementor), how support is built from the public hooks, and how a plugin ships its own.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/compatibilities/

Support for another plugin is a **compatibility**: a file that uses only the public [hooks](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/hooks/). The plugin ships three, for WooCommerce, Advanced Custom Fields and Elementor; any plugin can add its own — or replace the bundled one.

### At a glance

| Plugin | Status | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **WooCommerce** | Supported | Products, variations, orders and coupons as content types; shop, cart, checkout, my account and terms pages as linked settings; product galleries and category images; products shown by blocks suggested; product reviews in their own row; the product lookup table refreshed after an import |
| **Advanced Custom Fields (ACF)** | Supported (6.1 or later, free) | Its post types, taxonomies and field groups in its own export format, on their own row, imported before the content; fields that store IDs remapped; field groups and linked posts suggested; image and file fields as media used |
| **Elementor** | Supported (free) | Site settings (the Kit) and templates on their own row; pages' designs as `.json` files; all of it through Elementor's own exporter and importer, with images, templates and links remapped; templates and site settings suggested; generated CSS rebuilt |

### Advanced Custom Fields

Supported, with its own row: see [Advanced Custom Fields](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/advanced-custom-fields/). In short:

- **Post types, taxonomies and field groups** go in ACF's own export format and are imported before the content, updating the ones with the same key.
- **Field values** travel in the posts' and terms' custom fields; the ones that hold IDs (image, file, post object, relationship, page link, taxonomy, user) are **remapped** to the items on the other site.
- **ACF PRO** (repeater, flexible content, gallery, options pages, blocks) isn't covered yet; values on users don't travel (a WXR has no users).

### Elementor

Supported, with Elementor's own exporter and importer: see [Elementor](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/elementor/). In short:

- **Site settings** (the Kit) and **templates** go on their own row, in Elementor's formats, and come in through Elementor's own import; a later delivery updates them.
- **Pages built with Elementor** carry their design as `post_content/<slug>.json`, brought in by Elementor's document import, with images, templates and links pointing to the other site's items.
- **Elementor Pro** (Theme Builder, popups, forms) isn't covered yet; dynamic tags keep the IDs they hold.

Using another plugin and want it supported? [Open an issue](https://github.com/eizport/eizport/issues) with what you export — or write a compatibility, below.

### The WooCommerce compatibility

`includes/compat/woocommerce.php`, registered on `eizport_register_compat` when `WooCommerce` exists:

| Hook | Adds |
| --- | --- |
| `eizport_linked_options` | Shop, Cart, Checkout, My account and Terms and conditions pages, as roles |
| `eizport_option_groups` | The *WooCommerce pages* group |
| `eizport_denied_options` | `woocommerce_version`, `woocommerce_db_version` |
| `eizport_media_used` | Product and variation galleries (`_product_image_gallery`), and the images of the products' categories |
| `eizport_term_media` | Product categories' `thumbnail_id`, mapped to the imported image |
| `import_end` | Saves each imported product the way WooCommerce does and refreshes its row in `wc_product_meta_lookup` (prices, SKU, stock: what the shop's filters and sorting read) |
| `eizport_suggested_items` | Products that blocks and `[products ids="…"]` show in the items chosen |
| `export_wp` + `query` | Product reviews: only the ones chosen, when the export says which (`reviews`) |

### The Advanced Custom Fields compatibility

`includes/compat/advanced-custom-fields.php`, registered on `eizport_register_compat` when ACF 6.1 or later is active, and `includes/import-advanced-custom-fields.php` for the import:

| Hook | Adds |
| --- | --- |
| `eizport_content_types` | Leaves ACF's own post types out of the content rows |
| `eizport_look_items`, `eizport_look_data`, `eizport_look_suggested` | The *Advanced Custom Fields (ACF)* row: its items, their export (ACF's format) and what the posts chosen suggest |
| `eizport_media_used` | The attachments of image and file fields |
| `eizport_suggested_items` | The posts of post object, relationship and page link fields |
| `import_start` | Imports the post types, taxonomies and field groups (`acf_import_internal_post_type()`), and registers them |
| `import_end` | Maps the IDs in the values and in field groups' location rules |
| `wp_import_existing_post` | ACF's own posts in a WXR exist by key, not by title and date |

### The Elementor compatibility

`includes/compat/elementor.php`, registered on `eizport_register_compat` when Elementor is loaded, and `includes/import-elementor.php` for the import:

| Hook | Adds |
| --- | --- |
| `eizport_content_types` | Leaves Elementor's library (templates and Kits) out of the content rows |
| `eizport_look_items`, `eizport_look_data`, `eizport_look_suggested`, `eizport_look_media` | The *Elementor* row: the site settings and templates, their export (Elementor's formats), what the pages chosen suggest and the images they use |
| `eizport_content_file` | A page built with Elementor as `post_content/<slug>.json` |
| `wxr_export_skip_postmeta` | Its `_elementor_data`, `_elementor_page_settings` and `_elementor_css` out of the WXR, when the `.json` carries them |
| `eizport_media_used` | The images of the pages' designs |
| `import_end` | Templates, site settings and designs through Elementor's own import (`documents->create()`, the document's `import()`, the *Site_Settings* runner); the attachments marked so Elementor's import finds them; its CSS cache cleared |

### Writing one

```php
add_action( 'eizport_register_compat', function () {
	if ( ! class_exists( 'My_Plugin' ) ) {
		return;
	}
	add_filter( 'eizport_linked_options', 'my_plugin_eizport_linked' );
	add_filter( 'eizport_option_groups', 'my_plugin_eizport_groups' );
	add_filter( 'eizport_denied_options', 'my_plugin_eizport_denied' );
} );
```

`eizport_register_compat` fires on `plugins_loaded` at priority 20, after every plugin has loaded, so `class_exists()` checks are reliable.

### Replacing the bundled one

A plugin that ships its own support removes the bundled one first:

```php
remove_action( 'eizport_register_compat', 'Eizport\Compat\WooCommerce\register' );
```

### Testing

Test the compatibility's functions directly, so tests pass without the other plugin installed, and check that it registers only when that plugin is active.


---

## WP-CLI

> Export and import bundles from the command line with wp eizport export and wp eizport import, keep a delivery in a folder to compare, and run the abilities with wp eval.

Source: https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/wp-cli/

### wp eizport export

Exports as the Export screen does, to a copy kept on the site, and prints its path. Each run is a process of its own, so a script can make as many exports as it needs.

```bash
wp eizport export --types=page:43,product --options=basics,page_on_front
wp eizport export --types=page:43+44 --as-plugin --update-existing --filename=delivery
wp eizport export --types=page:43 --playground --themes=twentytwentyfive --plugins=woocommerce/woocommerce.php --landing=page:43 --language=pt_BR
wp eizport export --types=page --menus=classic:18 --filename=header
```

| Argument | |
| --- | --- |
| `--types=<types>` | Content types, comma-separated: `type:ID+ID` for some items, the type alone for all of it. None: all content |
| `--options=<options>` | Option groups (like `basics`) and option names, comma-separated |
| `--appearance=<parts>` | The site's [look](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/appearance/): `all`, or rows comma-separated, each whole or with its items' keys after a colon joined by `+` (`theme_mods:custom_logo+background_color,custom_css:r:1a2b3c4d5e`); with ACF active, `advanced-custom-fields` takes its [post types, taxonomies and field groups](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/advanced-custom-fields/) (`advanced-custom-fields:group_abc123+post_type_def456`); with Elementor active, `elementor` takes its [site settings and templates](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/elementor/) (`elementor:kit+t:28`) |
| `--css-mode=<mode>` | How the CSS rules are added on import: `end` (default), `start`, `replace` (the block of the same name; at the end with none) or `replace_all` |
| `--[no-]css-markers` | Head/tail comments around the CSS rules (default: Settings → Export) |
| `--menus=<menus>` | [Menus](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/menus/): `all`, or `classic:ID+ID` (menu term IDs) and `navigation:ID+ID` (`wp_navigation` IDs), comma-separated. None: no menus (all content already has them) |
| `--[no-]media` | Media files inside; default: yes |
| `--zip` | A `.zip` bundle instead of `.wxrz` |
| `--as-plugin` | A [plugin](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/as-plugin/) `.zip` that imports its bundle |
| `--update-existing` | Ask the import to [update the items that already exist](https://eizport.github.io/docs/getting-started/importing/#updating-items-that-already-exist) |
| `--playground` | A [Playground .zip](https://eizport.github.io/docs/formats/playground-zip/) instead of a bundle (not with `--as-plugin`, `--update-existing` or `--dir`) |
| `--themes=<stylesheets>` | With `--playground`: themes to install, comma-separated (a child theme brings its parent) |
| `--plugins=<files>` | With `--playground`: plugin files to install, comma-separated (`woocommerce/woocommerce.php`), active or inactive as on this site |
| `--mu-plugins=<files>` | With `--playground`: must-use plugins to write, comma-separated files of `wp-content/mu-plugins` (`cpt.php`), with the folders they load |
| `--landing=<where>` | With `--playground`: where it opens — `home` (default), `admin`, `page:ID` (saved as `/?pagename=<its path>`) or a path (`/shop/`) |
| `--language=<language>` | With `--playground`: the language it opens in — `site` (default), `user`, `en_US` or an installed locale (`pt_BR`) |
| `--filename=<name>` | File name, without extension |
| `--dir=<folder>` | Also write the bundle's files to a folder (see below) |

### A delivery in a folder

`--dir` writes the bundle's files to a folder: `manifest.json`, the WXR **formatted line by line**, `post_content/*.html`, `uploads/…` and `options.json`. The bundle files a previous export wrote there are replaced; other files (`.git`, notes) stay. Keep the folder under version control and `git diff` shows what changed since the last delivery — a title, a price — besides the export's dates.

```bash
wp eizport export --types=page:43,product --filename=delivery --dir=deliveries/site
git -C deliveries diff
```

The WXR in the folder keeps one name from one delivery to the next — `<--filename>.xml`, else `<site>.WordPress.xml`, without the date — so `git diff` shows what changed in it. The folder imports back with `wp eizport import <folder>`.

### wp eizport import

Imports a `.wxrz` or `.zip` bundle, a bundle folder (from `--dir`), a gzipped WXR (`.xml.gz`) or a plain `.xml` with the WordPress Importer — media from the bundle, `post_content/` files back in, options set at the end.

```bash
wp eizport import site.wxrz --user=admin
```

| Argument | |
| --- | --- |
| `<file>` | The file or bundle folder to import |
| `--user=<login>` | Who the posts go to; default: the first administrator |
| `--[no-]update-existing` | Update the items that already exist (same type and slug) instead of adding copies; default: no — the bundle never decides it on its own |
| `--options=<names>` | The bundle's options outside the [option groups](https://eizport.github.io/docs/exporting/options/#options-outside-the-groups-on-import) to set too, comma-separated; default: none |
| `--css-mode=<mode>` | How the bundle's CSS rules are added: `end`, `start`, `replace` (the head/tail blocks of the same name this site has; with none, at the end) or `replace_all`; default: what the bundle asks |
| `--[no-]css-markers` | Head/tail comments around them; default: what the bundle asks |

It needs the WordPress Importer plugin installed (it doesn't have to be active), in version 0.9.6 or newer; one newer than the version Eizport was tested with imports with a warning. A bundle made by a newer Eizport than this site's stops with an error that says which version it needs.

### Exporting with the ability

`wp eizport export` runs the [`eizport/export`](https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/abilities/#eizportexport) ability; to pass what it has no flag for (filters, reviews), run the ability itself:

```bash
wp eval '
wp_set_current_user( 1 );
$copy = wp_get_ability( "eizport/export" )->execute( array(
	"types"   => array( "page" => array( "ids" => array( 43 ) ) ),
	"options" => array( "groups" => array( "basics" ) ),
) );
echo is_wp_error( $copy ) ? $copy->get_error_message() : $copy["download_url"];
'
```

The copy is in `wp-content/uploads/eizport/tmp/`; one export per `wp` process.

### Other abilities

Any ability works the same way: `wp_get_ability( 'eizport/get-copies' )->execute()`, `wp_get_ability( 'eizport/delete-copies' )->execute( array( 'all' => true ) )`…


---

## FAQ

### Is it safe to import a bundle from someone else?

Only import files you trust, as with any WXR file. When a bundle is opened, only the files its manifest lists are written, only under a private folder, only with file types WordPress allows to be uploaded (never PHP), and never outside that folder. The folder is deleted when the import ends or is abandoned.

### Which plugins are supported?

WooCommerce, with its own support: products, orders and coupons, its pages as linked settings, product galleries, the products its blocks show (suggested) and product reviews. Advanced Custom Fields (ACF), with its own support too: its post types, taxonomies and field groups on a row of their own, in ACF's export format, imported before the content, and the fields that store IDs (image, file, post object, relationship, page link, taxonomy, user) remapped on import. Elementor, with its own support as well, through Elementor's own exporter and importer: its site settings (the Kit) and templates on a row of their own, each page's design as a .json file, and on import the images, templates and links inside them pointing to the items on the other site. The docs explain what to expect: https://eizport.github.io/docs/developers/compatibilities/

### What is an "as plugin" file?

A plugin .zip that holds the bundle. Install it on the other site (Plugins → Add Plugin → Upload Plugin) and click Run import on its row on the Plugins screen: it checks that Eizport and the WordPress Importer are there, imports the bundle with one click, and then offers to delete itself.

### Does it work on multisite?

Yes. Activate it on the network or on each site: every site exports and imports on its own (its files in its own uploads folder, its own saved defaults), links are mapped between subsites, and uninstalling cleans every site. Site administrators export and import; WordPress filters imported content for those who can't post unfiltered HTML. Docs: https://eizport.github.io/docs/getting-started/multisite/

### Is there a size limit?

Uploads are limited by your server's PHP settings (upload_max_filesize and post_max_size), which apply to the compressed file. A bundle may expand to 512 MB by default; developers can change it with the eizport_wxrz_max_bytes filter.

### Does it send data anywhere?

Not to its authors: Eizport has no service of its own. It uses WordPress.org's plugin and theme information and downloads, as WordPress does, and opens WordPress Playground only when you click to; see "External services" for what is sent and when. When importing a bundle, the importer's attachment downloads are answered from the bundle on your own server.

### What does the Playground blueprint do?

It installs the plugins and themes in the .zip, sets the language chosen (with its translations), writes the must-use plugins chosen (with the folders they load) and imports the WXR with Playground's own importer. With media or content files, they are written into Playground first and a temporary must-use plugin answers the importer's downloads from the media files and puts each .html file into its post, and a second one sets the settings when the import ends, with their IDs mapped; all of it is removed after the import. The WordPress Importer is installed by Playground itself, from WordPress.org.

### Who can download a Playground copy?

Anyone with its link: the file name ends in a random 16-character token, so it can't be guessed, and it is served only until it expires (a day by default; see the plugin's Settings, where it can also be "until deleted"), then deleted. On a site on your computer (like localhost), the link only works in your own browser. Don't keep copies of content that must stay private.

### Where are the files kept?

In wp-content/uploads/eizport/tmp/: Playground copies, and the folders of bundles being imported. Everything there is temporary, and the tmp folder itself is deleted once it is empty. Uninstalling the plugin deletes uploads/eizport/ and the plugin's settings.

### Where is the source code?

The PHP is in the plugin, readable. The Export and Settings screens' JavaScript in build/ is compiled; each file ships next to its unminified version, and its source (TypeScript, in routes/ and src/) is at https://github.com/eizport/eizport — build it with npm ci && npm run build (@wordpress/build).

---

## Changelog

### 1.1.0

- Added: Playground options: a Language group — the Playground .zip opens in the site's language (the default), yours or English, with the translations of WordPress, the themes and the plugins (fetched from WordPress.org, or this site's inside the .zip).
- Added: Block themes: templates and template parts edited in the Site Editor on rows of their own (Editor templates, Editor template parts), item by item with a preview. They travel in the WXR with the images they use; on import each replaces the same template of the same theme instead of adding a copy ("Header 2"), and its navigations, images and links point to the ones on the other site.
- Added: Elementor, with its own exporter and importer: a row of its own exports the site settings (the Kit) and templates in Elementor's formats; pages built with Elementor carry their design as post_content/<slug>.json; on import, Elementor's own import brings them in, with the images the bundle brought, templates and links pointing to the items there, and a later delivery updates instead of adding copies; also in Playground.
- Added: Advanced Custom Fields (ACF): a row of its own exports its post types, taxonomies and field groups in ACF's own export format, imported before the content (updated by key); the fields that store IDs (image, file, post object, relationship, page link, taxonomy, user) are remapped on import, also in Playground; field groups, linked posts and the media of image and file fields are suggested or come along.
- Added: Bundles say which Eizport made them and the oldest that reads them: a bundle that needs a newer Eizport is refused with a message that says which version (on the upload, wp eizport import, the import ability and a bundle plugin's screen, which offers Update now); bundles from 1.0.x still import. The WordPress Importer must be 0.9.6 or newer; a version newer than the tested one imports with a warning. The manifest names its JSON Schema (https://eizport.github.io/schemas/1.1/manifest.json): editors check a manifest edited by hand, and the import checks it against the same schema.
- Added: Multisite: each site of a network exports and imports on its own — saved defaults per site, files in the site's uploads, links mapped between subsites — and uninstalling cleans every site.
- Added: Export the site's look on rows of its own, item by item — Customizer theme mods and custom CSS rules, the Site Editor's style groups and CSS rules, widgets (classic and block) — with a preview of each and the media they use. On import, CSS rules are added to the other site's CSS (at the end, at the start, or replacing it) between head/tail comments named after the file; theme mods, style groups and widgets join the other site's instead of replacing them.
- Added: Export navigation menus on their own row — classic menus with their items and theme locations, and block navigations — and bring them back on import, pointing to the imported pages.
- Added: Playground options: must-use plugins — the ones chosen go in the Playground .zip with the folders they load, and the blueprint writes them before the import (not the platform's loaders nor Eizport's own).
- Added: Playground options: the button (renamed from "Themes and plugins") also sets where the Playground .zip opens — the home page, the dashboard, a page of the site (as a relative path) or a path —, its two groups open one at a time.
- Changed: The plugin's row on the Plugins screen keeps only Settings: no "Import .wxrz" or "Install the WordPress Importer" link — importing starts from Tools → Import.
- Changed: A bundle plugin's screen is one screen, with or without Eizport: Eizport is one more line in Before importing (Install Now, Activate or Update now, done right there), and what needs it waits — What it holds dimmed, Update existing and Run import disabled. The screen is no longer an item under Tools: Run import, on the plugin's row on the Plugins screen, opens it. Tools → Import lists it too, set apart from the other importers, and shows the list while it waits. "Update existing" names the content types the export holds — on the Export screen, the importer's step 1 and a bundle plugin's screen — and isn't offered with none.
- Changed: The Options row's Basics and Appearance groups no longer carry the theme mods (they have their own row) and now carry the block themes' site logo; imported theme mods are merged into the site's instead of replacing them.
- Changed: What a file holds no longer decides on its own: an import sets the options of the groups, the theme mods and the widgets, and any other option in the file only when whoever imports checks it (step 1 of the importer, a bundle plugin's screen) or names it (--options, the ability's options); WP-CLI and the ability update existing items only when asked. Options, theme mods and widget fields named like secrets (passwords, tokens, API and license keys) are never exported nor listed. On a network, a site administrator's Playground .zip takes only the plugins active on that site and the themes it may use.
- Changed: Bundles are plain .zip files by default (Settings → Export → "Bundle as .zip" now on), inside a plugin made as plugin too; turned off, they are .wxrz as before.
- Fixed: Imported content keeps working with its media and pages: the IDs in Image, Gallery, Cover, Media & Text, File, Video and Audio blocks, in navigation links and in block widgets point to the imported items, not to the other site's.
- Fixed: Links to the source site in imported content — pages, products, categories, navigation links, menus' custom links, widgets — point to this site after an import, in new and updated items.
- Fixed: An attachment the site already has gets its URLs in the imported content pointed to the file here on every import, not only with "Update existing" on.
- Fixed: Checked with the WordPress Importer 0.9.7: an edited image's link to its original is mapped on import instead of dropped (or left pointing at the exporting site's ID with 0.9.6).
- Fixed: The Playground .zip installs a theme or plugin from the WordPress.org directory only in a version the directory has; a development, beta or RC copy goes inside the .zip. Without Eizport, a bundle plugin installs it from the plugin directory.
- Fixed: An export of chosen types carries its terms in full — description, parent and term meta (a product category's thumbnail and display type), with their ancestors — not only their names.
- Fixed: The Playground .zip installs plugins active or inactive as they are on the site, instead of activating them all.
- Fixed: A .zip bundle is read in blocks against its real size (an entry that says it is small but inflates to more is refused, and no entry is loaded whole in memory), and needs PHP's ZipArchive; "Run import" only runs for a bundle plugin active on the site; the Playground landing page only opens a path of the exported site; uninstall also removes the note of imported widgets.
- Fixed: Importing a file made elsewhere is safer for users who may not post unfiltered HTML (a site admin on a network): templates, template parts and widgets from the file go through the same HTML filter as other content, custom CSS needs the right to edit CSS, Advanced Custom Fields items need ACF's own capability and never bring PHP callbacks, an existing page keeps its Elementor design unless the import updates existing items, and a malformed source address in the file never rewrites links.

### 1.0.1

- Scripts and styles of the classic Export screen, the importer and the Export and Settings screens are enqueued files.
- Keeping a Playground copy, which writes a file, needs the Export form's nonce.
- readme: an "External services" section on what is sent to WordPress.org, WordPress Playground and GitHub, and when.
